The MIR builder refuses `.into()` called straight on a unit-variant literal: `let b: B = A.Y.into();` checks (since eb790336d3), and `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run` stop with "a call with no resolved callee is not lowered yet", while `(A.Y).into()` prints `Q`
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: split from B-2026-10-21-80 (Thread A), whose check half landed in eb790336d3.

MEASURED on a llvm build of eb790336d3 with `enum A { X, Y } enum B { P, Q } impl From[A] for B { fn from(a: own A) -> B { match a { A.X => B.P, A.Y => B.Q } } } fn main() { let b: B = A.Y.into(); match b { B.P => println("P"), B.Q => println("Q") } }`: check passes; both MIR columns give `build: 5:16 in main: a call with no resolved callee is not lowered yet`. The call parses as `Call(Path([A, Y, into]))`. Check records the conversion through `try_apply_into_coercion` on a synthetic `MethodCall` at the call's span (`into_conversions` is keyed by that span), so the builder's `variant_builtin` / `variant_receiver` (src/mir/lower.rs), which cover `cmp`, `discriminant` and user methods on this shape, need the conversion too. Owner: Thread B (MIR builder).
fix: da0b9e8019: the call of the path `A.Y.into` reaches the builder with no resolved callee; before refusing it, `variant_into` (src/mir/lower.rs) now builds the unit variant the first two segments name and calls the user's `From` impl for the call's type (`user_from`), lending or moving the variant as `from`'s parameter takes it. MEASURED: the row's program prints Q on `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run`; a borrowing `fn from(a: A) -> N` into a struct prints 2 on both and on `__mir-llvm-asan`. Pinned by a_unit_variant_converts_through_its_from_impl (tests/mir_variant_into.rs); control on 26a0cb8378's lower.rs: 0 passed, 1 failed with "a call with no resolved callee is not lowered yet". Gate: default `--all` 9444 passed, llvm 9339 passed, both clippy legs clean. Not covered: `A.X.into()` into `A` itself, which check refuses (no reflexive `From`, none in the spec).

title: A closure returned from a closure is tied to the callee: `let make = |n: i64| |x: i64| x + n; fs.push(make(i));` is refused by check and both MIR columns (E0509 "the result borrows `make`"), though §9.3 makes a returned closure own its captures and the same shape through `fn adder(n: i64) -> Fn(i64) -> i64` passes
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found by Thread A triaging the corpus entries bucketed b-fix-incomplete:E0516 (fixtures/memory_sanitizer/closures/asan_curry_closure_vec_store_no_leak, expected output 100).

MEASURED on a llvm build of eb790336d3: `fn main() { let make = |n: i64| |x: i64| x + n; let mut fs: Vec[Fn(i64) -> i64] = Vec.new(); let mut i: i64 = 0; while i < 200 { fs.push(make(i)); i = i + 1; } println(f"{fs[100](0)}"); }`: check gives `7:9: the result borrows make, which this function owns, so it would outlive it (core-semantics.md §5.4) [E0509]`, and `__mir-run` / `__mir-llvm-run` give `borrow check main: 7:9: a view of _2 is stored in an escaping closure, a shared value or a channel` [E0509]. `let f = make(3); println(f(1))` (not stored) passes and prints 4. `fn adder(n: i64) -> Fn(i64) -> i64 { |x| x + n }` with `fs.push(adder(2))` passes and prints 3. core-semantics.md §9.3: a closure that is returned escapes and captures every place by move, so the inner closure owns its copy of `n` and borrows nothing of `make`. Check's message is the MIR borrow check's (src/mir/borrowck.rs), relayed. Also seen: the AST escape walk (src/core_escape.rs) walks a closure body's tail as `Pos::Other` while a `return` in the body is `Pos::Escape("returned")`; making the tail escape alone does not clear the refusal. Owner: drop schedule (MIR borrow check).
fix: eede6bfd40. A closure body is called directly with its environment first (`main.c0(&make, i)`), and `result_borrows` gave program bodies `Args`, so the result borrowed `&make` and storing it in `fs` escaped that loan (E0509; check relays the MIR borrow check). Core semantics §9.3: a returned closure escapes and captures by move, so it can hold what the environment holds but never the environment itself. Lowering now records the closure bodies whose return type is a function (`Lowered::closure_results`, src/mir/lower.rs), and `result_borrows` gives them the new `ResultBorrows::EnvAndArgs` (src/mir/borrowck.rs `transfer_call`): what the environment points to (or holds, when it is passed by value), plus the other arguments. A reference the outer closure captured still ties the result to its referent: writing the referent while the result lives is E0516, and storing the result where its borrow is not kept is E0509. The row's program passes check and prints 100 on `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run`. Pinned by tests/mir_closure_results.rs (5 tests, in ci.yml's llvm list). Control, the same tree with the new arm disabled by an env gate: 3 passed, 2 failed (the row's program and a moved `String` argument); the other three are guards. Gate: fmt, both clippy legs, wasm clippy, `cargo test --all`, `cargo test --features llvm` (failures only the known mir_par_for_iterations_wait_concurrently timing flake and the regex tests with no opt-in archive), msrv, and the `closure`-tagged corpus on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan (no failure in a closure-returning body). Not covered: a returned closure that captures one of the outer closure's own non-`Copy` captures, which check passes and the MIR build refuses; filed separately.

title: A borrow-check refusal names a MIR temporary: `let f = make("abc".to_string());` with `fn make(p: String) -> Fn(i64) -> i64 { |n| p.len() + n }` reports "drop of _2 while it is borrowed (borrow at 3:13) [E0516]" on check, where the reader needs the temporary `"abc".to_string()` and the binding `f` that borrows it
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found by Thread A triaging the corpus entries bucketed b-fix-incomplete:E0516 (fixtures/codegen/closures/heap_env_mixed_pod_string_capture_runs, now `v2_reject`: the refusal itself follows the current reading, where the returned closure is a view of its borrowed parameter `p`).

MEASURED on a llvm build of eb790336d3: `karac check` prints `error[typecheck]: f.kara:3:5: drop of _2 while it is borrowed (borrow at 3:13) [E0516]`, and `__mir-run` prints `borrow check main: 3:5: bb2[term]: drop of _2 while it is borrowed (borrow at bb1[0] at 3:13) [E0516]`. Check relays the MIR borrow check's message (src/mir/borrowck.rs), so `_2` and the basic-block positions are internal. Binding the argument first (`let s = "abc".to_string(); let f = make(s);`) passes and prints 8. A message in the shape of check's own E0516 ("cannot drop the temporary `"abc".to_string()` at the end of this statement while `f` still borrows it ... bind it to a variable first") would say what to do. The same `_2` shows in B-2026-10-24-9's MIR message. Owner: drop schedule (MIR borrow check), with Thread A for check's relay.
fix: 94e7ecf4ae. Re-measured on a llvm build of 3d092a40bd: the row's program no longer reaches the MIR relay on check. Since 5f1a515ae0 (B-2026-10-25-20) the front end refuses it first ("an escaping closure captures `p` by move (core-semantics §9.3), but `p` borrows its value"), and the general case, a `let` keeping a borrow of a temporary, has typecheck's own §5.5 message ("a reference to a temporary outlives its statement ... Bind the temporary to a variable first"). `karac check` on all 2126 corpus programs whose expectation is a refusal printed no `_N` and no block position. The relay's fallback could still pass a temporary's MIR name through, so: a BorrowError now carries `temporary`, where a temporary place's expression is (src/mir/borrowck.rs `temporary_at`), and check's E0516 for one reads "cannot drop the temporary value of the expression at L:C while `f` still borrows it (the borrow is taken at L:C; core-semantics.md §5.5) [E0516]. Bind the expression to a variable first, so the value lives as long as the borrow" (src/cli.rs `mir_check_message`); any other MIR text reaching check reads a temporary's place (`_2`, `(*_2).1`) as "a temporary value" (`mir_check_text`). `__mir-run`'s own message still names `_2`: it is the corpus backend's, not a user surface. Pinned by src/cli.rs mir_message_tests (2 tests).

title: A `match` on a tuple of handle LOCALS that outlive it (`match (top_left, top_right, bottom_left, bottom_right) { (Quad.Leaf(p), ..) => .. }`, kata 558's `intersect`) still counts each handle into the built tuple and releases the tuple after the match, although the arms only read discriminants and Copy payloads
detail: SOURCE NOTE: the remainder of B-2026-10-23-13, split at its close (a97412f163). That fix reads a scrutinee tuple's parts straight from the borrowed PARAMETERS they copy (kata 951's shape), which is sound because a count-safe body with no `mut ref` parameter cannot change what a `ref` parameter points at. Kata 558 builds `_30 = (move _31, .., move _34)` from `_31 = retain(_17)` .. `_34 = retain(_26)` over LOCALS that stay alive and are used after the match (`Quad.Split(top_left, ..)`). Reading `_30.i` as `_17` etc. also needs each source to be neither assigned, moved nor dropped between the tuple's definition and its last read, which is a dataflow fact rc_borrow does not compute today (it checks whole bodies). The row's measurement stands: removing the other 8 count sites moved kata 558's bench by noise only (1.99-2.10 s to 1.97-2.05 s), and v2 already beats legacy there. So this is low; a lowering that matches element places directly when the scrutinee is a tuple expression of places would remove it for every source kind at once.
fix: ea9c109f6e: the builder matches `match (a, b, ..)` over locals' places where the parts lie, when every arm is `_` or a tuple pattern that binds only `Copy` values by copy, and every guard is plain operators over names (src/mir/lower.rs `scrutinee_parts`, `copies_only`, `test_parts`/`bind_parts`). A part must be `Copy` or a handle (`shared`), which the tuple only counted. A `ref` part is seen through. No tuple is built, so no handle is counted into one and released after the match: kata 558's shape and the param shape alike. Any arm binding a handle or a `ref`/`mut ref`, or any other guard, still matches a built tuple, so no binding outlives the match without its own count. tests/mir_tuple_match_in_place.rs pins the in-place shapes and the fallback (interpreter and built binary; output checked against a Python mirror). The control arm on fb7694c88b's lower.rs fails it (0 passed; 1 failed: "merge builds a tuple"), with the same program output. src/mir/rc_pairs.rs `mir_rc_pairs_moves_a_handle_into_the_returned_value` flips from 2 retains in `two` to 0. Measured: 196 corpus programs with a tuple match, on mir-interp and mir-llvm, gave no new reds (the 6 reds are stale legacy expectations). Kata 558 on mir-llvm-asan: 5 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip. The drop schedule's pin program is clean under ASan. As the row measured, the bench effect is within noise.

title: `karac fix` has no fix for `format!("..{}..", a, b)`: the error names the f-string to write but offers no edit, though a literal whose holes are all `{}` or `{:spec}` with one argument each maps one-to-one onto `f"..{a}..{b:spec}.."`
fix: 80fb30bcf3 gives the parse error the edit that writes the f-string: src/parser.rs format_macro_rewrite replaces `format!(..)` with `f"..."`, each `{}` / `{:spec}` hole taking the next argument's text and `{{` / `}}` carried over. There is no fix when the first argument is not a one-line `"..."` literal (raw, triple-quoted or a variable), when a hole names its argument (`{0}`, `{name}`), when its spec is not one FormatSpec::parse accepts (`{:?}`), when the counts disagree, or when an argument's text holds a quote, a brace, a `:`, a backslash, a comment or a line break. The parser now carries the source text (Parser::with_source, set by karac::parse, parse_at_offset and parse_items_only), since this fix moves argument text into the literal. The row's repro goes through `karac fix` to `let s = f"bias {n + 1}, n {n:03}";` and prints `bias 4, n 003`. Pinned by tests/format_macro_fix.rs (the rewrite, which reparses clean and runs, plus nine refusals). The B-2026-10-20-5 pin in tests/parser.rs, which held that format! got no fix at all, is flipped to expect the f-string edit. Control on the pre-fix tree: both rewrite pins fail; the refusal pin passes there because the old tree offers no fix for anything.

title: The turbofish fix deletes `::<T>` / `::[T]` from `let x = it.collect::[Vec[char]]();` and leaves `let x = it.collect();`, which then fails E0238 "cannot infer type parameter 'C'": in a `let` with no annotation the fix should move the type onto the binding, as its own message tells the author to (fixed for `collect` / `sum` / `product` only, deliberately: other methods keep the delete-only fix)
fix: 51f56fc2ed makes the turbofish fix two-sided when the call is the whole initializer of a `let` binding one name with no annotation: Parser::reject_method_turbofish (src/parser/exprs.rs) records each turbofish with its method and the list's Kāra spelling (turbofish_binding_type: `<Vec<char>>` is `Vec[char]`), and parse_let_statement's move_turbofish_to_binding (src/parser/stmts.rs) replaces the delete-only edit with a fix_diffs pair that also inserts `: T` after the name. The row's repro is fixed to `let marks: Vec[char] = "ab".chars().collect();`, and the bracket form, `sum::<i64>` and `product::[i64]` likewise. Deliberately narrower than the row's remedy: only `collect`, `sum` and `product` move the type, because their type argument is what they return; `"4".parse::<i64>()` (whose result is a Result) and any other method keep the delete-only fix, as do a `_` placeholder (`Vec<_>`, which an annotation does not accept), several type arguments, a call inside a larger expression or an argument, a destructuring pattern and an annotated binding. Pinned by tests/turbofish_fix.rs (the four rewrites reparse clean and run to `2 3 6 6`, plus six delete-only cases); the B-2026-10-06-126 pins in tests/parser.rs are unchanged. Control on the pre-fix tree: the rewrite pin fails, the delete-only pin passes there as it should.

title: A growing `VecDeque` moves its elements into the new buffer one at a time on the compiled backends: RawDeque::grow (runtime/src/mir.rs) computes each slot with `%` and copies each element with a runtime-sized memcpy call, so kata 958's breadth-first bench, a fresh queue per call whose head has marched round before it grows, spends 2.9B of 11.3B instructions there and runs 2.2x Rust
detail:
B-2026-10-13-36 put push, pop and indexing in line and left growth in the runtime (`karac_mir_deque_push` when len == cap). The growth loop is

    for i in 0..self.len {
        copy_nonoverlapping(self.slot(i, size), buf.add(i * size), size)
    }

with `slot` doing `(head + i) % cap * size` and the copy a memcpy call through the PLT, because `size` is a runtime value.

Kata 958 (check completeness of a binary tree), bench program: 200 trees of up to 100 nodes, 4000 rounds of the first-gap walk, each call a new `VecDeque[Option[TreeNode]]` that pops at the front while pushing two children at the back, so it grows about six times per call from a wrapped ring. Release karac at dcb1e820c2, cachegrind: 11.31B instructions, 102.9M indirect branches (one memcpy call per moved element); karac_mir_deque_push 1.75B and __memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms 1.16B. Eight runs: 1.07 to 1.19 s; Rust (`VecDeque<Option<Rc<RefCell<TreeNode>>>>`, rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on) 0.46 to 0.74 s, median 0.55 s; C with a stack ring 0.10 s.

A full ring is the run head..cap then the run 0..head, so two bulk copies move it.
fix: d34614d017. RawDeque::grow now moves a full ring into the new buffer with two bulk copies, the run head..cap and then the run 0..head, instead of one `%` and one runtime-sized memcpy call per element; an empty buffer (cap 0) copies nothing. detail: Found writing kata 981 (Time Based Key-Value Store, kara-katas leetcode/901-1000/981-time-based-key-value-store), whose natural first draft was `fn set(mut ref self, key: String, value: String, timestamp: i64) { self.store.entry(key).or_insert_with(Vec.new).push((timestamp, value)); }`. Probe on main 3a35c05fbb (debug karac, `karac check`), one struct with `store: Map[String, Vec[(i64, String)]]`, `log: Vec[(String, i64)]`, `plain: Vec[String]` and three methods taking a bare `key: String`: (1) `self.store.entry(key)...` -> `expected 'String', found 'ref String': a borrowed value cannot be moved out of what it borrows. Take an owned copy with `.clone()`` (no mention of the parameter, no `own` fix); (2) `.push((timestamp, value))` on that entry -> `expected '(i64, String)', found '(i64, ref String)'` with no hint at all; (3) `self.log.push((key, timestamp))` -> `expected '(String, i64)', found '(ref String, i64)'`, no hint; (4) `self.plain.push(key)` -> `cannot give away parameter `key`: a bare parameter borrows (core-semantics §4.1), and an owned 'String' is wanted here. Take it by value with `key: own String`, or hand on a copy with `.clone()`` (the B-2026-10-24-19 fix working). So the same mistake, a bare parameter given to an owned slot, gets the give-away message and `own` fix only when it is the whole argument of push/insert; inside a tuple literal, or as the key of `Map.entry` (an `own K` parameter), it gets the generic mismatch. A user writing the natural form sees three different errors for one cause, and the tuple ones name no remedy. The kata ships with `key: own String, value: own String`, which is the right signature; the gap is only the diagnostic.

fix: 3a38fff707 widens the followers that let Parser::recover_keyword_as_ident (src/parser.rs) retype an escapable keyword as the `r#` identifier its fix writes. In a pattern, `in` (a `for` binding), `=>` and a guard's `if` (an arm) and `@` now follow a name; anywhere, the bitwise operators `&`, `|`, `^`, `<<` and `>>` do too (the kata's `if and & x == 0`). Without them the `for` and arm sites returned None, and the recovery that followed skipped a closing brace: hence `Expected expression, found RightBrace` and the false top-level-statements error at a statement inside `main`. The row's probes now give only the reserved-keyword error, once per occurrence, and the `r#and` fixes leave a program that parses and runs. Pinned by tests/keyword_binding_recovery.rs (ten uses of `and` across a for tuple pattern, a bare for binding, a plain arm, a guarded arm, an `@` arm and a bitwise operand: ten errors, the fixed source runs to the expected output). Control on the pre-fix tree: the pin fails.
title: A reserved keyword (`and`) bound by a `for` loop, or as a match-arm pattern, gets the right "reserved keyword" error and then cascade errors: `Expected expression, found RightBrace` and, for the loop, a false `file contains both top-level statements and an explicit fn main()` that points at a statement inside `main`
detail: Found writing kata 982 (Triples with Bitwise AND Equal To Zero), where a loop over a map of pair ANDs was first written `for (and, count) in pairs { if and & x == 0 { triples += count; } }`. `karac check` gave the correct first error (`'and' is a reserved keyword and cannot be used as an identifier; write `r#and``) at the pattern and again at the use, then three more: `expected `;` after this expression statement` at the function's tail `triples`, `Expected expression, found RightBrace` at the function's closing brace, and `file contains both top-level statements and an explicit `fn main()` (defined at line 30); move the statements into `main`...` pointing at `triples`, a statement inside a function. Probe on main 3a35c05fbb (debug karac, `karac check`), one statement inside `fn main()` between `let`s and a `println`: `let and = 1;`, `let (and, b) = (1, 2);`, `for (and, b) in w {}`, a closure `|and: i64| and + 1` and a parameter `fn f(and: i64)` each give only the reserved-keyword error(s), one per occurrence. `for and in v {}` gives it and then `Expected expression, found RightBrace` at main's closing brace and the false top-level-statements error at the `println` inside main. `match 3 { and => {} }` gives it and then `Expected expression, found RightBrace` at the arm's `}`. So recovery after the error is clean in let, tuple, closure and parameter patterns but not for a bare `for` binding or a match-arm pattern, and in a larger body the bad recovery can also hit a later use of the keyword in expression position (`and & x`), where `and` parses as the operator. The first error is right and names the fix; the rest are noise, and the top-level-statements one is false. Parser files have not changed between 3a35c05fbb and 46a460bc2b except 9b5f87b927 (select).

detail:
SOURCE NOTE: reported by Thread B (cross-session message, 2026-10-24) while reading the statement verdicts; katas 245 and 310 have the same shape. Owner: kata thread (src/mir/effects/).

`branch_uses` (src/mir/effects.rs) computes the "leaves" blocks of a branch, those that can only reach Return, and skipped them whole: `for &b in set.difference(&leaves)`. That is right for a `?` arm, whose blocks only drop what is live and write the result, but an arm written `if c { let mut t = 0; for x in v.iter() { t = t + *x; }; return t; }` lowers entirely into blocks that can only reach Return, so the loop's reads of `v` were never recorded. The Dependence and Conflict checks then saw no use of `v` in the second statement, and the verdict grouped it with the `fill(mut v, 100)` before it.

Repro (unit test auto_par_statement_that_returns_still_uses_what_it_reads, functions `go` and `near`): on the control (origin/main d867340a02) both get a Statements verdict with groups; the test fails 0 passed; 2 failed with its sibling below.

title: Auto-par statement verdicts (`KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1`) let a statement that may panic run beside an earlier one that may return, so `if grow(n) < 10 { return -1; } let g = grow(lines[1]);` is grouped and the second statement's panic can end a run the first statement's return would have let go on
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: reported by Thread B (cross-session message, 2026-10-24), from apps/pipeline/index_build parse_index@391; B also pointed at the both@56 pin in tests/mir_auto_par.rs. Owner: kata thread (src/mir/effects/auto_par.rs).

`stopped(i, j)` refuses a group when branch i stopping first would hide something branch j does. For a returning i it counted j's caller-visible writes and escapes only. A panic in j is just as observable: in order, the return keeps j from running at all, so the program goes on; run together, j may panic and end the program. The panic case (`panics[i]`) already counted visible effects; the return case left out j's own `panics`.

Repro (unit test auto_par_statement_that_may_panic_stays_after_a_return, function `second`): the control groups the pair; the fix refuses it with Stops{visible: 1, effect: "panics"}. In tests/mir_auto_par.rs, mir_auto_par_statement_groups_match_in_order's `both` and `early` stay in order for this reason, and its pin loses them.

title: Indexing a `Map` with a missing key (`m[k]`, `m[k] -= 1`) stops with `runtime error: explicit panic` under `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run`, a message that names no key and reads as if the program had called `panic`, where an out-of-range `Vec` index says `index out of bounds`
fix: 216cc03ccc gives the missing-key panic its own message, the same on both backends: `key not found`. The interpreter's `("index" | "index_mut", [key]) if is_map` arm (src/mir/interp.rs) sets the panic message to KEY_NOT_FOUND before it aborts, and src/backend/mir/table.rs's arm passes the same text to abort_unless (agreed with the drop schedule, which owns the file). The row's repro now stops with `runtime error: key not found` / `at mk.kara:4:13` under `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run`, exit 101. The key is not printed: a byte-identical message on both backends would need a display of the key in the compiled one, and Rust's own map index does not print it either. Pinned by tests/mir_map_missing_key.rs (a read, a compound `m[k] -= 1` on a `Map[String, i64]` and a `SortedMap` read, on both backends; added to the ci.yml llvm list). Control on the pre-fix tree: the pin fails.

title: A built program dies with exit 141 (SIGPIPE) when it writes to a child's stdin after the child exits; the MIR interpreter returns an error from the same write
detail: Measured at e17192b260. `let child = Command.new("true").stdin(Stdio.piped()).spawn().unwrap(); let w = child.stdin().unwrap(); let _ = child.wait(); match w.write_all(Vec.filled(65536, 7).as_slice()) { Ok(_) => println("wrote"), Err(_) => println("write failed") } println("survived");` prints `write failed` / `survived` under `karac __mir-run`, exit 0, and nothing under `karac build --mir`, exit 141. The interpreter is a Rust program, whose start up sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN; a compiled `main` skips that start up, and the MIR runtime never ignores the signal (the legacy event loop did, runtime/src/event_loop.rs, only for sockets). Sockets are unaffected: std sends with MSG_NOSIGNAL (a write to a hung-up TcpStream fails on both backends). Pipes use write(2), so the write raises SIGPIPE.
fix: e09926a988 makes the MIR runtime ignore SIGPIPE once, before the first child with a piped stdin starts (runtime/src/mir_process.rs ignore_sigpipe, a plain signal(2) call, so the lean archive needs no libc), as Rust's own start up does for the interpreter. The write then fails with an error on both backends: the row's program prints write failed / survived, exit 0, under karac __mir-run and the built binary alike (it was exit 141 built). std's Command resets the child's disposition before exec, so the child still gets the default. tests/mir_process_sigpipe.rs pins both backends (control at e17192b260: 0 passed / 1 failed, the built run exits 141).

title: v2 prints no error return trace for a `?` chain: `main` returning a propagated `Err` prints `Error: e` alone on both backends, and a panic's trace is only its own location, though design.md § Error return traces records each `?` site on the way (2 cli tests ignored)
detail: The remainder of B-2026-10-23-18, split at its close. design.md § Error return traces: in debug builds each `?` site pushes `(file, line, col)` on `Err` and clears on `Ok`; the trace is printed with the diagnostic. On v2, `fn inner() -> Result[i64, i64] { Err(7) }`, `middle` = `inner()?`, `outer` = `middle()?`, `main() -> Result[(), i64]` = `outer()?` prints `Error: 7` (exit 1) on `karac run`, `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run`, with no trace; a panic prints `Error return trace:` with only the panic location as its frame. The runtime already has the ring buffer (`karac_error_trace_push` / `_clear`, runtime/src/lib.rs § Error return trace) with an atexit printer; the MIR builder emits no call at a `?` site and the interpreter has no buffer. Ignored tests: tests/cli.rs test_error_return_trace_is_deterministic_across_runs and test_error_return_trace_is_complete_without_the_pool. Those two pin legacy's printer, which wrote the trace at exit whenever the buffer was non-empty, even after `main` handled the error with a `match`; the spec says the trace goes with the diagnostic, so decide which when fixing. Owners: Thread B (`?` lowering), drop schedule (backend calls), Thread C (interpreter natives).
fix: f2ff086fc1 (v2 prints the error return trace of a `?` chain). The builder calls `error_trace_push(line, col)` on a `?`'s error path and `error_trace_clear()` on its success path, for a `?` in the program's own source; `karac build --release` strips both (KARAC_STRIP_ERROR_TRACE). The MIR interpreter and the runtime (a thread-local trace of string-constant places, runtime/src/mir.rs) keep 64 frames, and print them after `main`'s `Error: e`; a panic's trace is the recorded frames, then its own place. A succeeding `?` costs one unordered load of the module's count of threads with frames, which a loop hoists. Decision on the row's question: the trace goes with the diagnostic, as design.md says, not at exit after a handled error as legacy printed it; the two cli tests now propagate out of `main` (3 frames; json.kara's cases then a failing parse, with and without KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1), and run_v2's JSON pin now expects the frame. tests/mir_error_trace.rs pins the chain, the clear, the panic, truncation and the release strip on both backends. Remainders: JSON `expr`/`context` fields (B-2026-10-25-29) and the split-across-tasks note (B-2026-10-25-30).

title: A package with more than one module is checked without D5: its per-module passes and late phases read a bare parameter as owned, so the check in front of `karac run` / `karac build` refuses a call a lone file accepts (`value 's' moved here, used again here` after passing `s` to a bare `String` parameter)
fix: f36a5e4595. `package_check_on` (src/cli/build_cmds.rs) rewrites every module's bare parameters with `d5_params::borrow_bare_params` over the package whole (`borrow_bare_params_of`: an impl borrows where its trait in another module does, a `Copy` type from any module or the library copies) and checks each module under `strict_core`, so the per-module passes and the flattened late phases read a bare parameter as the borrow the v2 check of the combined source does. The row's repro checks and runs (`5 abc`); a callee giving its bare parameter away is refused in its own file. On the examples' packages the per-module check now refuses exactly the places `karac run` refused on the combined source (db_pipeline: the same 16), and slipstream's three false moves out of a collection element are gone. `run` and `build` on a package (`run_v2::combine`) now leave a type or late-phase refusal of the module-aware check to `check_v2` on the amalgam, which renders it with relative paths, snippets and fixes; the module-aware refusal (`Amalgam::refusal`) prints only if that check passes, and parse, cycle and resolve refusals still stop the command at once. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_package_with_two_modules_reads_a_bare_parameter_as_a_borrow` (control at d9f5d6b067: 0 passed, 1 failed). Flipped: tests/cli.rs `test_build_project_late_phase_diagnostic_includes_file_context` and `test_check_project_reports_the_multi_file_ownership_error_build_reports` take their moved parameter `own`.

title: `karac check` on a package with more than one module runs only the module-aware package check, not the v2 check of the combined source that `karac run` and `karac build` run after it, so check passes a package that run and build refuse (examples/db_pipeline: `All checks passed.`, but `karac run` refuses `cannot move 'row'` at src/db.kara:105:64)
detail:
Measured at 3c10118a4d and before it. `karac run` / `karac build` on a package call `run_v2::combine` (gate: `gate_run_on_package_check`, the per-module check) and then `check_v2` on the amalgam (`Pipeline::new(..).strict_core().with_library()`, diagnostics remapped through `Amalgam`), src/cli/run_v2.rs. `cmd_check_project` (src/cli/run_check_cmds.rs) prints the per-module `PackageCheck` and stops. So every core rule the per-module passes do not apply (borrow_projection_copy, D5 borrows, the library's methods) is reported by run and build but not by check.

Repro: `cd examples/db_pipeline && karac check` prints `All checks passed.`; `karac run src/main.kara` prints `error[borrow_projection_copy]: src/db.kara:105:64: cannot move 'row': it borrows its value ...`, then fifteen more at src/planner.kara, src/executor.kara (`cannot give away ... a bare parameter borrows`, a `par` block of statements at executor.kara:76:9). Likely fix: after a clean `PackageCheck`, `cmd_check_project` combines the package (`project_v2::amalgamate`) and runs the same check `check_v2` runs, without exiting on its own; an amalgam refusal (a renaming import, B-2026-10-23-14) is then reported by check as by build.
fix: 3baf757f4d. `cmd_check_project` (src/cli/run_check_cmds.rs) now combines a package with more than one module (`project_v2::amalgamate`) and runs the v2 check `karac run` and `karac build` run on it (`run_v2::check_v2_or_exit`, split out of `check_v2`), its text and JSON diagnostics named by the package's files. As in `run_v2::combine` (B-2026-10-25-4), a type or late-phase refusal of the module-aware check is left to that check first; parse, cycle and resolve refusals are reported alone, and a package that cannot be combined is refused by check as by build. examples/db_pipeline now fails check with the same 16 errors `karac run` prints, and on every example package check and `run --interp` print the same errors (weave, a one-module package, is checked as a lone file). Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_package_check_refuses_what_the_v2_check_of_its_combined_source_does` (control at 62020a628f: 0 passed, 1 failed). The fixture's loop over a borrowed parameter showed a separate check gap, B-2026-10-25-25.

fd8b172278 (src/typechecker/patterns.rs `infer_collection_elements`). An array or `Vec` literal now meets its elements the way an `if`/`else` join meets its branches: when either side still carries an inference variable they unify and the joined type carries on, and a slot one element leaves open (`None`'s `T`, `Vec.new()`'s element) takes the other element's type through `join_branch_types`. Only a pair that is neither open nor joinable reaches `check_assignable`, so a real mismatch (`[Vec.new(), Some(1)]`) is still refused. Corpus check sweep: no new fails; package compare: all 9 SAME.

With `#[derive(Clone)]` on `Tok` the row's program is fixed in one pass and prints 1; without it the type has no `.clone()` and there is no fix. The length and capacity arguments of `Vec.filled`, `Vec.with_capacity`, `VecDeque`/`String.with_capacity`, and their siblings in src/typechecker/expr_call.rs and the check-mode arms in src/typechecker/exprs.rs go through `check_i64_arg`, which runs the sign-changing-coercion check a user call runs after `check_assignable`, so a `usize` length is refused with "implicit coercion from 'usize' to 'i64'", and a `v.len() as usize` one gets B-2026-10-25-10's drop-the-cast fix. fix: 2928490eee (src/typechecker/closures.rs `walk_capture_consume`, src/typechecker/patterns.rs, src/mir/lower.rs `owned_node`). The closure-kind walker now reads all three uses as reads. (1) A user method's argument borrows unless the parameter is `own`, decided from the receiver's type through `d5_own_params`, as the `Call` arm decides a free function's. (2) A captured `shared` handle used as a value is counted, not moved (`copy_is_only_an_rc_retain` at the identifier leaf, §6.1). (3) A `match` consumes its scrutinee only when an arm binds a part that could move. The pattern check now records such scrutinees on both pipelines (`moving_scrutinees`), counting a bare type parameter's value as a move. The MIR builder's capture walk read a typed-HIR `shared` ADT (an `Adt`, not `Shared`) as owned and moved the handle into the closure; `hir_handle` now counts it. Pin corpus/core/ok_closure_reads_method_args_handles_and_matches passes on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan. Test `a_closure_that_lends_counts_or_matches_a_capture_stays_fn` checks and runs the row's program to "15 10 3 5", and still refuses a method's `own` parameter and an arm that moves a part. Control arm at a6d57a78ee: 0 passed; 1 failed; fix arm: 1 passed. Corpus check sweep: no new fails. Package compare: all 9 SAME. The shared-field write that makes a closure `MutFn` (the row's unclaimed note) is B-2026-10-26-10.
title: The closure-kind walker calls three uses that move nothing a consume, so the closure is `OnceFn` and refused for an `Fn` slot: a capture passed to a user METHOD's parameter (bare or `ref`), a captured `shared` handle used as a value, and a `match` on a captured place whose arms bind nothing by move

fix: 1b9edf0601 (src/use_classifier.rs `note_capture_scope`, src/cfg.rs `UseSite::capture_scope`, src/rc_predicate.rs `in_capture_scope`). An escaping or task closure captures by move (§9.3), and the use classifier made every use of a capture in its body a consume, so the second `size(prog)` was a use after a move. The capture moves in once, at the closure's creation. A use that is a consume only because its closure captures by move (a read in the body) now carries that closure's span. The use-after-move, reuse (RC) and loop-of-consume predicates pair it with no later use inside the same closure, so reading the capture twice, in both arms of an `if`, or in a loop checks. A use after the closure is created ("moved into an escaping closure") and a real move in the body followed by a read are still refused. Pin corpus/core/ok_escaping_closure_reads_its_capture_again (two reads, a loop, a task) passes on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan. Test `an_escaping_closure_reads_its_capture_again`. Control arm at 8f312bbd5c: 0 passed; 1 failed; fix arm: 1 passed. Corpus check sweep: no new fails. Package compare: all 9 SAME. Found on the way: an escaping closure created inside a loop is not caught at all, filed as B-2026-10-26-11.
title: `karac check` reports a capture of an ESCAPING closure as moved by its first use inside the body: two `size(prog)` calls (`p: ref Prog`) in one escaping closure are 'value prog moved here, used again here', while both MIR backends accept the program and print the right answer

fix: fda9e3a216. The `Op` derive is the right first step, not a wrong type: with `Op` `Copy`, `karac fix` derives `Clone` on `Prog` on its next run and writes `prog.clone()` on the third, after which the program checks and prints `2 2` (an `eat(prog)` twice variant; the row's own r4.kara no longer errors since B-2026-10-25-14). What was wrong is the hint's claim that the derive makes 'prog' copied. The typechecker now records which derive fix-its are a first step: the moved value's type reaches more than one type needing a derive (`copy_derive_first_steps`, src/typechecker/derives.rs `derive_names`). The ownership pass words those as "add `#[derive(Copy)]` to 'Op' (its fields are all `Copy`), the first of the derives 'prog' needs before it can be cloned (`karac fix` adds the next one)" through one helper, `derive_advice` (src/ownership.rs), shared by the three E0500 hint sites. A type that a single derive makes `Copy` still says the value is copied. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_nested_derive_fix_is_named_a_first_step` (the hint, then three `karac fix` runs reaching a program that checks; control at cb53ae1d38: 0 passed, 1 failed).

The tests still ignored with `v2 gap after M3: the v2 project build does not report this yet (legacy project-build output)` or `... does not print the dependency summary` (tests/cli.rs): test_build_project_lists_discovered_modules, test_build_project_rejects_panic_unwind, test_single_file_build_refuses_package_member, project_build_wasm_target_selects_wasm_platform_module, test_build_project_missing_src_dir_fails, test_build_project_json_output, test_build_project_requires_entry_file, test_build_project_empty_src_dir_fails, test_build_project_json_includes_resolve_diagnostics, test_build_target_from_manifest_build_section, test_xpkg_import_typechecks_and_builds, test_xpkg_transitive_path_dep_resolves. fix: 1ed4f406c2: the v2 package build (src/cli/build_v2.rs cmd_build_v2_project) reports and refuses what the legacy project build did. Text mode prints the package summary before `Built:` (project, edition, root, target, entry, each module with its platform, and `deps:` with each dependency package), and `--output=json` carries the same fields (`project`, `edition`, `root`, `target`, `entry`, `modules` with path/role/platform/file, `diagnostics`) with `status` and `output`, with and without the llvm feature. The walk and the tree now run before the entry check, so a missing `src/`, an empty one and a package with no entry file get the walker's and the tree's own refusals; `[profile] panic = "unwind"` is refused (the backend is abort-only); the walk follows `--target`, so `wasm_wasi` takes the `_wasm` platform modules. The typechecker now records the uses it reports for a binding it offers `: Str` (`str_retyped_uses`, in `explain_str_lit_lets`), and the ownership pass drops a use-after-move whose move or reuse is one of them (src/ownership.rs, before the result is built), taking the contradicting `.clone()` fix-it with it. g1.kara now reports only the four type errors; one `karac fix` run writes `let s: Str` and the result checks and prints `1 1`. `karac check` accepts an ESCAPING closure that uses a bare (borrowed) non-Copy, non-handle parameter as a whole (`new_op(|x| x + size(p))`, `p: P` with a `String` field): the closure can neither move it out of the borrow nor outlive it, so v2 captures the reference and it dangles
fix: 5f1a515ae0. The use classifier (src/use_classifier.rs, `note_escaping_borrow_capture`) records a place an escaping closure uses from behind a borrow (a bare or `ref` parameter, a `ref` local) that is neither `Copy` nor a counted handle, and check refuses it (src/ownership/rc_promote.rs) as 'an escaping closure captures `p` by move (core-semantics §9.3), but `p` borrows its value, so `p` cannot be moved out of it', suggesting `own` or a clone before the closure: the row's `new_op(|x| x + size(p))`, the same over `p: ref P`, and a non-`Copy` field (`|x| x + p.s.len()`). A `Copy` field (`|x| x + p.n`) is still copied and runs (`6 7`). On the way, src/core_escape.rs read any `Path` call without a signature as an enum variant constructor, so a closure passed to a built-in such as `Vec.from_fn` in a function's tail counted as returned (escaping); only a call on a known enum is a constructor now. The corpus check sweep is unchanged except six legacy closure fixtures in corpus/fixtures/codegen/closures that returned a closure over a bare parameter, which take it `own` now with the same output. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `an_escaping_closure_cannot_capture_a_non_copy_place_behind_a_borrow` (three refusals; the Copy field, an `own` parameter and `Vec.from_fn` run; control at 3eda032ac8: 0 passed, 1 failed).

title: On the MIR interpreter, a group's deadline never tears down the task that ran last before it fired: that task is marked cancelled but stays parked, and the run stops with a deadlock error
detail: Measured at c46d884d71. `let (tx2, rx2): (Sender[i64], Receiver[i64]) = channel(1); let c = TaskGroup.new().with_deadline(Duration.ms(20)); let k = c.spawn(|| match rx2.recv() { Some(v) => v, None => -1 }); match k.try_join() { Err(TaskFailed.Cancelled) => println("k cancelled"), _ => println("other") }` stops under `karac __mir-run` with `error: deadlock: every task waits on a channel that no running task sends to or receives from`; §11.10 says the deadline cancels the task, so `k cancelled`. The executor fires deadlines between tasks (`fire_deadlines` at the top of `run_tasks`), but `cur_task` still names the task that ran last, here `k`, parked on its `recv`. `cancel_group` takes that task for the running one, marks it cancelled for its next wait and does not tear it down, so nothing ever wakes it. tests/mir_deadline.rs's with_deadline test passes only because a sleeping sibling runs last.
fix: c2f859dacc. `fire_deadlines` cancelled the group while `cur_task` still named the task that ran last, so `cancel_group` took that task for the running one, which a cancel skips, and it was left suspended with its group waiting on it: a deadlock. It now sets `cur_task = usize::MAX` while it cancels, as no task is running at that point, and restores it after. Pinned by `tests/mir_deadline_last_task.rs` (mir_deadline_tears_down_the_task_that_ran_last), which hung before the fix.

title: `IsolatingGroup.spawn` of a named function (`g.spawn(work)`) is refused at build with `an isolating group's spawn of other than a closure written there is not lowered yet`; `karac check` accepts it
detail: Found writing M4 item 9 (core-semantics §11.12). The MIR builder lowers an isolating group's `spawn(f)` to the group's `TaskGroup.spawn` of `f`'s own closure with its value wrapped in `Ok` (`isolating_spawn` in src/mir/lower.rs: `closure_ret` and `closure_exit`, as a `par` branch's task is built), which needs `f` to be a closure literal at the call. `fn work() -> i64 { 7 } fn main() { let g = TaskGroup.isolating(); let h = g.spawn(work); println(f"{h.join().is_ok()}"); }` type-checks and fails at build; `|| work()` works. The remedy is presumably a wrapper task body for a function value (the coroutine transform's `task_body` builds one by hand for closures).
fix: 6fcffec0b3. The builder runs a function value as an isolating group's task through a synthesized `own || f()` closure (`isolating_task_expr` in src/mir/lower.rs), which `isolating_spawn` lowers as it does a closure written at the call: its value in `Ok`, a panic the handle's `Err`. A function named by path is called directly, so a panic in it reaches the task's cancel exit; a generic function or another value is called through. Pinned by tests/mir_isolating_fn_value.rs (named function, associated function, closure variable, function parameter; refused at build on the control). Not covered here: a call through an ERASED function value (one picked at run time) is not yet a cancel point, so a panic in it still ends the process; the drop schedule folds that arm into cancel_point with its M4 item 4. A generic function as a value is refused at build everywhere ("a generic function as a value is not lowered yet"), isolating or not.

title: v2 does not mark a panic raised while a `requires`/`ensures` predicate is evaluated (inline or in a callee) as `contract predicate panicked: ..`, so `karac test` reports it with no `contract_predicate_panicked` category (1 cli test ignored)
detail: The remainder of B-2026-10-23-15. test_test_failure_emits_contract_fault_category (tests/cli.rs): `fn at(v: ref Vec[i64], i: i64) -> i64 requires deref_at(v, i) { 0 }` with `deref_at` indexing out of bounds reports `"message":"index out of bounds"` with no category; design.md § Contracts rule 2 and src/cli/test_cmd.rs's contract_fault_category want `contract predicate panicked: index out of bounds` -> `contract_predicate_panicked`. `contract_violated` already works (0bb0c20d38). Plan: the builder brackets each predicate with natives `contract_enter` / `contract_exit` (src/mir/lower.rs contract_check_here); the interpreter keeps a depth and prefixes any panic or fault raised above depth 0; mir-llvm maps the natives to the runtime's existing karac_runtime_enter_predicate / _exit_predicate (runtime/src/lib.rs) and the v2 panic printer prefixes when the depth is non-zero. Touches interp natives (Thread C) and src/backend + runtime (drop schedule); asked both 10-25.
fix: f82c28e5e9: the builder brackets each `requires` / `ensures` predicate with natives `contract_enter` / `contract_exit` (src/mir/lower.rs contract_check_here). The MIR interpreter counts the depth and marks an abort raised above 0, in the predicate or in a callee, as `contract predicate panicked: <msg>` in abort_message, which both report_abort and an isolating group's contain() read; mir-llvm calls the runtime's existing karac_runtime_enter_predicate / _exit_predicate (src/backend/mir/call.rs), and karac_mir_abort / _abort_at mark the message the same way (runtime/src/mir.rs abort_message). The row's program reads `contract predicate panicked: index out of bounds` on __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run, ASan and the built binary; test_test_failure_emits_contract_fault_category un-ignored (contract_predicate_panicked and contract_violated both reported). Fixture tests/mir_contract_predicate.rs (the callee case fails at control 03f4a34e2e). The 149 runnable corpus programs with a contract give the same pass/fail as before (the 8 fails are `old` and type invariants, not lowered).

title: `karac check` accepts `with_provider[Clock](FakeClock {..}, ..)` and `Clock.now()` when the program redeclares `effect resource Clock;` and `FakeClock` implements no `ClockProvider` (only an inherent `now`); the same program without the redeclaration, and a trait-less user resource of any other name, are refused per §14.1, and the MIR builder stops on it
fix: 16eec2e53b. A program's own `effect resource Clock;` (or `Env`, `RandomSource`) shadowed the library's declaration with a trait-less one, so `with_provider[Clock](FakeClock {..}, ..)` skipped the provider-trait check and the MIR builder then stopped on `Clock.now()`. The redeclaration is now a type error in src/typechecker/env_build.rs (strict core, outside the library) naming the library's declaration and trait, with a machine-applicable fix that deletes it; the provider check then runs against `ClockProvider`. The row's program is refused with both errors; with `impl ClockProvider for FakeClock` `karac fix` deletes the line and the program prints 42. Two corpus copies of tests/cli.rs fixtures that still had the old shape moved to the spec form the tests use. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs a_program_cannot_redeclare_a_library_resource (control at 578e9c3467: 0 passed; 3 failed with the -26/-33 pins). Corpus check sweep identical to the base.

title: WIDER THAN FILED: `karac check` accepts a method taking `own self` on ANY borrowed receiver (a `ref` parameter, a bare one, a bare `for` element of a borrowed collection, a user `own self` method on `x: ref S`), which the MIR builder refuses; filed as: `karac check` accepts a move out of a bare `for` element when the collection is a bare (borrowed) parameter: `fn total(v: Vec[Option[String]]) -> i64 { for o in v { n += o.unwrap().len(); } }` checks, though the same loop over `v: own Vec[...]` is refused (E0515 'a bare `for` borrows it, and this method takes `self` by value') and `karac run` refuses it at MIR build
fix: 5e1f7f9923. The use classifier (src/use_classifier.rs) passed an `own self` receiver by copying when the receiver's type was `Copy` or counted, and a `ref T` is `Copy`, so a method taking `own self` on any borrowed receiver read it: `o.unwrap()` on `o: ref Option[String]`, on a bare parameter (D5) or on a bare `for` element of a borrowed collection, and a user `x.take()` on `x: ref S`, were accepted by check and refused by the MIR builder. The test now looks through the borrow at the value the method takes, so these are the §3.7 error 'cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place: this method takes `self` by value' with its `.clone()` fix, while `o.unwrap()` on a `ref Option[i64]` still copies. The corpus check sweep is unchanged (3926 failing directories before and after, the same set). Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `an_own_self_method_on_a_borrowed_receiver_is_a_move_out_of_the_borrow` (four shapes refused then fixed, plus the Copy case run; control at c7fc7a9814: 0 passed, 1 failed).

title: `karac fix` on a file of a package fixes it as a single file: it cannot see the package's other modules, so a resolver 'did you mean' rewrites a correct name to an unrelated one (`Enum(n)` -> `Env(n)` in a `match` on an imported enum) in a program `karac check` and `karac run` accept
fix: 66683e8bf5. `karac fix` on a module of a package (not a lone src/main.kara) now takes its fixes from the package (src/cli/fix_cmds.rs package_member_fixes): a resolve refusal's from the package's own per-module resolve, otherwise from the v2 check of the combined source that `karac check` and `karac run` make, mapped back to the file through the amalgam's byte map. A fix applies in the module its edits land in; an import is added only to the module whose use asks for it; other modules' fixes are named in a note. Package resolve fixes also carried offsets in the tree's rebased span range (module.rs #46), so the JSON `replacement` of a non-first module pointed past its file; each Module now records its span_base and resolve_modules rebases the edits. The row's package: `karac fix src/main.kara` leaves `Enum(n)` alone. selfhost: three fix passes per file take `karac check` from 217 errors to 100, all `.clone()`/`own`/`ref`/derive/`.ok()` edits, no renames or imports. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs karac_fix_on_a_package_module_fixes_it_from_the_package_view. Follow-ups: B-2026-10-25-34 (imported `take` typed as the library's), B-2026-10-25-35 (combined-source places in package diagnostics and JSON).

title: A function type's effect clause with commas between its effects (`Fn(A) -> R with writes(Stdout), receives(Network), blocks`) ends the struct field, tuple element or `type` alias at the comma with `Expected Colon, found LeftParen`; the space-separated clause parses (the `receives(Channel)` half is B-2026-10-25-40)
detail: Found writing tests/mir_fn_values_suspend.rs (M4 item 4). `struct Job { run: Fn(ref Receiver[String]) -> String with writes(Stdout), receives(Channel), blocks }` gives `error[parse]: Expected Colon, found LeftParen` at `receives(`; `run: (Fn(..) -> String with writes(Stdout), receives(Channel), blocks)` gives `Expected RightParen, found LeftParen`; `type JobFn = Fn(..) -> String with writes(Stdout), receives(Channel), blocks;` gives `Expected Semicolon, found Comma`; `with a + b` and space-separated verbs do not parse either. A single effect (`with suspends`) parses, and `karac build` then demands every effect of the stored function in the slot (`field `run` has effect writes(Stdout) not declared in slot [suspends()]`), so the only stored callbacks that build are those with one kind of effect. design.md §12 (Function values and effects) writes the clause as on a fn declaration (`with reads(Log)`); a multi-effect clause needs a grammar that a field list or a generic argument list does not split. Related: `receives(Channel)` named in a clause is refused by the resolver (`'Channel' is not an effect resource (it is a prelude type or trait)`), though the effect checker reports the slot's missing effect under that name.
fix: 7eba43e706. The parse half. The space-separated clause already parsed in a struct field, a tuple and a `type` alias (`Fn(i64) -> String with writes(Stdout) sends(Network) blocks`); the row's claim that space-separated verbs fail was refuted: what failed there was the resolver refusing `receives(Channel)`, now its own row B-2026-10-25-40. Commas between the effects (`with writes(Stdout), sends(Network), blocks`) ended the field at the comma (`Expected Colon, found LeftParen`); a comma inside a function type's clause followed by a built-in verb with its resource list, or by a bare `blocks` / `suspends` / `panics` not followed by `:`, now gets the declaration clause's "effect items are space-separated" diagnostic and its machine-applicable delete edit, so `karac fix` writes the space-separated form. A comma that ends the field, tuple element or parameter (`, blocks: i64`, `, Fn(i64) -> i64`) still ends it. A stored callback declared with several effects (`writes(Stdout) sends(Network) receives(Network) blocks suspends`) checks, runs and builds. Pins: tests/fn_type_effect_clause.rs (4 tests). Control arm at 51abd5e206: the comma test fails, the other three pass.

title: A spawned closure that moves one half of a destructured tuple into an array literal (`group.spawn(|| count([rx]))` after `let (tx, rx) = channel(1)`) makes the checker treat the other half as borrowed by the task: a later `let _ = tx;` is refused with `tx is moved while a task of group borrows it`
fix: e121bf2159. The array literal was not the cause. The TaskGroup pass (src/typechecker/core_taskgroup.rs) declared every name a `let` pattern binds at the pattern's own span, so `tx` and `rx` of `let (tx, rx) = channel(1)` were one place there. The task's borrow of `rx` (the array literal is not one of `moved_in`'s move forms, so `rx` counts as borrowed, while `count2(rx)` counts as moved) then covered the later use of `tx`. Each binding is now declared at its own leaf span (`binding_name_spans`), in `let` and `let ... else`. The row's program checks and prints `1`; a task capturing `a` of `let mut (a, b) = ..` leaves `b.push(9)` free (prints `2 2`), while `a.push(9)` with the group open is still refused under §9.5. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_task_capturing_one_half_of_a_tuple_let_leaves_the_other_free` (control at 7ffa426d55: 0 passed, 1 failed); tests/mir_cancel.rs passes. Corpus check sweep and the 9-package compare unchanged.

title: The error return trace's JSON frames carry `file`, `line` and `column` but not design.md's `expr` (the `?` expression's text) or `context` (a `.context()` message), on both v2 executors
detail: Split from B-2026-10-25-3 at its close. design.md § Errors (the error-return trace) and § Error return traces show each frame as `{"file", "line", "expr": "db.find(id)?", "context": "while loading user 42" | null}`. v2's `karac run --output=json` / `jsonl` (src/cli/run_v2.rs Report::emit) parses the text trace, whose frames are `file:line:col`, so it can emit only file/line/column, as legacy's runtime printer did. The text form would need the expression (the builder has the `?`'s span, so the source slice) and a `.context()` site's message; the JSON then reads them back.
fix: 42614fb9d9: Each `?` in the program's own source that returns an error now pushes the expression as written, its whitespace collapsed to one line, beside its place: src/mir/lower.rs error_trace passes the source slice of the `?` expression as a third argument; the interpreter (src/mir/interp.rs) and the compiled backend (src/backend/mir/call.rs) print the frame as `file:line:col  expr`; src/cli/run_v2.rs reads it back and every JSON / JSONL frame carries `"expr"` and `"context": null`. Measured: tests/mir_error_trace.rs (5 tests, interpreter, `__mir-llvm-run`, `karac build`, `--release`) and tests/run_v2.rs run_v2_json_output_carries_the_runtime_reports pin the text on both executors; on the control (0a8255be80's src with these tests) mir_error_trace is 0 passed; 5 failed. A two-file package names each frame's own file and expression. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE (partial): `context` is always null, because the v2 library has no `.context()` or `AnyError` (B-2026-10-21-22); filling it once `.context()` exists is B-2026-10-25-44.

title: A `?` chain that crosses a task boundary prints the frames left on the exiting thread instead of design.md's `Error return trace: unavailable (the ? chain was split across parallel tasks)`; waits on M4 item 10's pool
detail: Split from B-2026-10-25-3 at its close. The trace is per thread (runtime/src/mir.rs ERROR_TRACE, the interpreter's error_trace). Until M4 item 10, v2 tasks run cooperatively on one thread and a `?` chain never suspends mid-propagation, so the output is deterministic, but a chain carried out of a task by a join (the task's `Err` `?`-ed by the parent) shows the parent's frames plus whatever the task's frames left after other tasks' successful `?`s cleared them, not the whole chain and not the note. design.md § Error return traces: report the chain as unavailable when it ran across `par` branches or TaskGroup tasks. Owner: Thread B with item 10 (a worker pool makes the split real).
fix: e790115219 gives each error-trace frame the task that pushed it: the compiled runtime records crate::mir_task::current_task() beside each frame in runtime/src/mir.rs ErrorTrace, and the interpreter records its cur_task in src/mir/interp.rs. A `?` that succeeds clears only its own task's frames, since another task's chain may still be on its way. A trace whose frames come from more than one task prints design.md's `Error return trace: unavailable (the ? chain was split across parallel tasks)` instead of a fragment, and `karac run --output=json|jsonl` reports it as a trace with frames [] and an "unavailable" reason (src/cli/run_v2.rs). Pinned by tests/mir_error_trace_tasks.rs on both backends and both run lanes (control on main: 2 of 3 fail with the old fragment). The test is added to CI's llvm list. Known limit: a task that handles an error with a match and then finishes without a later successful `?` leaves its frames behind, so a later chain in another task reads as unavailable. That is the conservative answer, and the same staleness a handled error already has within one task.

title: A table's hasher is not part of its type on v2, where collections.md makes `H` the last type parameter of `Map[K, V, H]` / `Set[T, H]`: the parser strips it, so a table built without the annotation in sight walks in the seeded order, and no BuildHasher's own code runs (a user hasher's build/write/finish never run, and an Fx table hashes with SipHash). RULED 10-27 by the review thread: `H` becomes a real type parameter. Stage 1 is the type, with the default filled in where `H` is omitted; stage 2 runs the builder's code. Already fixed: annotated lets, plain struct fields, returns, owned params, shared fields, and qualified constructors (5ed688429b)
detail: Split from B-2026-10-24-29 at its close (legacy parity: legacy honoured the hasher only on an annotated `let` too). v2 keeps the hasher as one bit per table (src/mir/lower.rs names_a_hasher + the `table_unkeyed` builder native; runtime/src/mir_map.rs MirMap.unkeyed; the interpreter's unkeyed_tables): such a table walks under karac_hash::walk_perm_by(n, hash_u64_unkeyed), so its order is fixed across processes, which is the only observable effect design.md § Hash and Hasher gives a pinned hasher (the index hash itself is internal). Remaining: (1) a user hasher's `build`/`write`/`finish` are not called, so a hasher with side effects or a deliberately colliding digest behaves as the default; calling them from the table glue needs B-2026-10-25-32 (a method call on `B.Hasher` in a generic fn does not lower). (2) IntrinsicTy::Map/Set still carry no hasher, so the bit is set at the `let` and carried by clone (karac_mir_map_like / clone_unkeyed), but a table built in a struct literal field, returned from a fn, or passed to a parameter typed `Map[K, V, H]` keeps the seeded walk. Repro: `struct S { m: Map[i64, i64, FxBuildHasher] }` then walk `s.m` in two processes: the order moves. Update (Thread B, struct fields): a plain struct's field whose `Map` / `Set` type names a hasher now marks the table the struct literal stores there and the table an assignment to the field stores (src/mir/lower.rs hashed_field / unkey_table; tests/mir_hasher_fields.rs, which fails on the control binary). A `shared` struct's field is not marked: its literal builds a handle, and the field place sits behind it. B-2026-10-25-32 is fixed (2fb98ebc8d), so part (1) is no longer blocked; it is observable only through side effects in the hasher's own methods, since the index hash is internal. Update (Thread B, returns, params, shared fields): a function whose declared return type names a hasher marks the table it returns (its tail and every `return`), an owned parameter so typed marks its table on entry, and a `shared` struct's literal marks the table before it stores it (src/mir/lower.rs return_exit, lower_fn_inner, the StructLiteral arm; tests/mir_hasher_returns.rs, which fails on the control binary at 29bcb98e49). Still open: (1) as above, and a borrowed parameter or a turbofish, which hand on a table built elsewhere. Update (Thread B, 10-26): the remainder needs the hasher in the type. The parser strips it from `Map[K, V, H]` into a span-keyed side table (container_hashers), so the checker's and MIR's types are `Map[K, V]`; a table built anywhere unannotated keeps the seeded walk, e.g. `let mut b: Vec[Map[i64, i64, FxBuildHasher]] = Vec.new(); b.push(Map.new())` walks b[0] in a different order under KARAC_HASH_SEED=1, 2 and 3, and the turbofish `Map[i64, i64, FxBuildHasher].new()` is refused by the checker (cannot construct `Map[?T0, ?T1]` as `Map[i64, i64, FxBuildHasher]`). Update (drop schedule, 10-27): 5ed688429b makes `Map[K, V, H].new()` / `Set[T, H].new()` record and validate their hasher as a type does, and their table walks in a fixed order (tests/mir_hasher_turbofish.rs). RULING (review thread, 08:04Z): option A, staged. `Map[K, V, Fx]` is a different type from `Map[K, V]`, as Rust's HashMap<K, V, S> is, and generic code over any hasher writes `Map[K, V, H]` with `H: BuildHasher`. Stage 1 carries H through the checker, MIR types and both backends; stage 2 calls the builder's Kāra code, with a fast path for the two library builders if measurements call for one. If stage 1 stops many corpus programs from type-checking, report the count to the review thread before migrating. Site inventory (read-only sweep): about 97 sites assume Map[K, V] / Set[T] (checker 34, MIR 45, backend 10, other 8), about 35 of them non-mechanical. The riskiest: mir/ty.rs's (Map, [k, v]) arm, which turns a 3-arg map into Other silently; lower.rs's element-tuple and 1|2-arity matches; unification arity; lowering.rs display_map_types; impl-head matching; and the stdlib impls (collections.kara, serde.kara), which are all `impl[K, V] Map[K, V]` and must become generic over H.

fix: 2fb98ebc8d. fix: 581bf59ec2. All five servers (Server.serve, serve_static, serve_tls, serve_ws, serve_ws_tls) are Kāra in runtime/stdlib/source/http_server.kara: the accept loop is a task, and each connection it accepts is a task of an isolating group (core-semantics §11.12) that answers the client's requests in order, pipelined ones included, and keeps the connection while the client asks to (`Connection: close`, or HTTP/1.0 without `keep-alive`, ends it). A client that stalls mid-request holds only its own task; a handler that panics ends only its own connection; a WebSocket session runs in its connection's task. The current request is per task on both backends (the interpreter keys it by task; the runtime keys MIR_REQUESTS by mir_task::current_task() with an on_task_end hook), and the native one-at-a-time server (http1::Server, karac_mir_http_bind/next/respond) is gone. Pinned by tests/mir_tls_ws.rs mir_serve_answers_connections_concurrently_with_keep_alive on both backends (control: fails on 2d6e5f5772). serve's bind failure now reads as the other servers' (`bind failed: invalid input`; SERVE_UNBOUND updated). Found on the way and fixed in the same commit: an isolating task that panicked after its first wait ended the process on the interpreter (tests/mir_isolating_after_wait.rs). Review-thread ruling: the handler stays Fn(Request) -> Response, so corpus todo-api (and its kara-katas source, backend/todo-api/main.kara) and examples/shortener, which passed a MutFn, keep their state in a `shared struct` with `mut` fields; that is sound on today's single-threaded executor, and M4 item 10 decides whether such state must be `sync` once connection tasks run on threads. E_RAII_ACROSS_YIELD (withdrawn, §11.9) left the pipeline in the same push; its dead code is B-2026-10-25-50. Rows filed from this work: B-2026-10-25-47, -48, -49, -50.
title: Server.serve/serve_tls/serve_ws/serve_ws_tls serve connections one at a time; a stalled handshake or request blocks the accept loop (fixed with keep-alive for all five; serve's bind-failure text deliberately changes to the other servers' `invalid input`)
detail: Review-thread ruling 2026-10-25 18:02Z on M4 item 8 (4b274d9189): accepted for M4a since it matches `serve`, but design.md's services track and core-semantics §11.12 assume one task per connection. Today `serve` (native, src/http1.rs) reads, answers and keeps alive one connection before accepting the next; the three in runtime/stdlib/source/http_server.kara answer one request per connection (`connection: close`) sequentially, with only upgraded WebSocket sessions as tasks. So a client that stalls its TLS handshake or its request head holds up every other connection. Target: each connection a task of an isolating group (a handler panic ends only its connection), with keep-alive for all four. Prerequisite: item 9's compiled half (isolating groups on `karac build`). Also needed: `Request` reads one process-wide current request (the interpreter's `http_request`, the runtime's thread-local `MIR_REQUEST`), so concurrent handlers that suspend need the request carried per connection (a handle in `Request`). Until then docs/library/io.md § HTTP server says requests are served one at a time.

Program: `shared struct Plain { n: i64 }` / `sync struct Holder { p: Plain }` / `fn read(h: Holder) -> i64 { let q = h.p.clone(); q.n }` / `fn main() { let h = Holder { p: Plain { n: 1 } }; let g = TaskGroup.new(); let t = { let h1 = h.clone(); g.spawn(|| read(h1)) }; println(f"{t.join()} {h.p.n}"); }`. `karac check` prints `All checks passed.` (checked on 101333c368 plus item 10a). title: An error return trace frame's `context` is always null: design.md § Errors fills it from a `.context(msg)` site's message, but the v2 library has no `.context()` or `AnyError` (B-2026-10-21-22), so no site can carry one
detail: Split from B-2026-10-25-29 at its close (42614fb9d9). design.md § Errors (the error-return trace): "A site with `.context()` fills `\"context\"`; a bare `?` leaves it `null`." Since 42614fb9d9 each frame of `karac run --output=json` / `jsonl` carries `"expr"` (the `?` expression's text) and `"context": null` (src/cli/run_v2.rs RuntimeReports::emit). Once `AnyError` and `.context()` exist (B-2026-10-21-22, Thread A), the `?` on a `.context(msg)` receiver needs its message in the frame: the builder would pass it as a fourth `error_trace_push` argument (it is a runtime value, unlike the expression text, so the backend's frame cannot stay a constant string), the text trace would print it, and run_v2 would read it back. Blocked on B-2026-10-21-22.
fix: 0bd9d73105: a `?` whose operand is the library's `.context(msg)` on a `Result[T, AnyError]` passes a `ref` to the message that call just pushed onto the error's context list, as a fourth `error_trace_push` argument (src/mir/lower.rs `trace_context`; the callee must be the library's `context`, so a program's own method of that name fills nothing). The MIR interpreter and the runtime (new `karac_mir_error_trace_push_context`, which copies the message into the frame) write it after the frame's expression as `  context: MSG`, with `\` and newline escaped. `karac run --output=json` / `jsonl` read it back into the frame's `"context"`, and a bare `?` stays `null` (design.md § Errors). `--release` records no trace, as before. `context` joins library_prune's ALWAYS_KEPT, because the builder names it. tests/mir_error_trace_context.rs pins the text trace on the interpreter and the built binary, the JSON frames, and the program-method case. The control arm on dd5e90a747's src and runtime fails both tests (0 passed; 2 failed). The probe programs are clean under `__mir-llvm-asan`.

e0e2a6f136: ruled by design.md § Cycles and `weak`, which passes a strong handle "where a `weak` type is expected": a `weak` parameter or local is storage like a `weak` field. A strong handle stored into it is downgraded, and a read upgrades it to `Option[T]`, `None` once the object is gone. Checker (src/typechecker/exprs.rs, the Identifier arm): a read of a `weak` local or parameter, not an assignment's target, is typed `Option[T]`, as fields.rs types a `weak` field read; so passing a `weak` local on to a `weak` parameter, `cur = c.parent` and `match w { Some(n) => .. }` check. Builder (src/mir/lower.rs): expr_ty reads a `weak` local or a borrowed `weak` parameter as the `Option` of its referent, expr_place upgrades it (through the parameter's reference when it is borrowed), count_copy stores a strong handle into a `weak` local as a downgrade through a borrow (it had retained the strong handle into the weak slot), and a struct literal into a `weak` local is built in a temporary and downgraded. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_weak_local_reads_as_option (spec, rule 6.5): interpreter, mir-llvm and ASan pass; on the control (the src of e0e2a6f136's parent at the time, a pre-rebase tree) check refuses it with "cannot store value of type 'weak Node' into a `weak Node` field". The 53 corpus entries that use `weak` give the same verdicts as before (two stale legacy-run expectations, WEAK_STORES and 432's bench, fail as they did). NOT DONE, the row's second half: `.upgrade()` on a `weak` slot (`a.me.upgrade()` is still "no method 'upgrade' on type 'Option'"), which Thread A will take later. Also seen: passing a `weak` field straight to a `weak` parameter (`id_of(a.me)`) is refused by check as a move out of a borrowed place.
title: A `weak T` local (`let w: weak N = a;`) passes `karac check` but every MIR backend refuses it: "a type that failed to check is not lowered yet" at its first use
detail: Found writing tests/mir_sync_counts.rs (M4 item 10a-2). Program: `shared struct N { id: i64, mut me: weak N }` / `fn main() { let a = N { id: 1, me: Option.None }; let w: weak N = a; println(f"{w.is_some()}"); }`. `karac check` prints `All checks passed.`; `karac __mir-run` fails `error[mir]: build: 4:35 in `main`: a type that failed to check is not lowered yet` (the column of `w`'s use), and so does `w.upgrade()`. title: In a package of several modules, the package check's per-module typecheck refuses what the v2 check of the combined source accepts, and its refusal stands: a `ref` to an IMPORTED `shared` enum ("expected 'E', found 'ref E'", which B-2026-10-25-12 fixed for a lone file) and `f64.parse(s).ok()` ("no method 'ok' on type 'Option'": it types `parse` as returning `Option`, not docs/library/core-types.md's `Result`)
detail: Measured at ae8ea6fbb5 (after 92a0f23874). Package `demo`: src/ast.kara = `pub shared enum E { A(i64), B }`; src/main.kara = `import ast.{E};` / `fn size(e: E) -> i64 { match e { E.A(n) => n, E.B => 0 } }` / `fn main() { let v = Vec[E.A(4), E.B]; let r = ref v[0]; println(f"{size(r)}"); }`. `karac check` and `karac run src/main.kara` refuse `main.kara:11:21: expected 'E', found 'ref E'` [E0200]. The same two files concatenated into one (import dropped) run and print 4. So the refusal comes from the package check's per-module typecheck (src/cli/build_cmds.rs typecheck_modules), where `E` is an imported name; the v2 check of the combined source accepts it. This blocks the self-hosted compiler's port (B-2026-10-23-20): 97 of its 99 remaining errors are this shape, for `pub shared enum Expr`, `TypeExpr`, `Pattern` (selfhost/src/ast.kara) and the plain struct `Span` (6 sites; a plain struct is not a handle, so those 6 are the port's to fix by hand). Owner: Thread A (check). ADDED 2026-10-25: the same mechanism refuses `f64.parse("1.5").ok()` in any package of two modules (src/u.kara = `pub fn one() -> i64 { 1 }`, main imports it): `no method 'ok' on type 'Option'` [E0200], while a lone file runs it and prints 1.5; the self-hosted lexer has 2 such sites (selfhost/src/lexer.kara:521, :531). The per-module refusal is kept on purpose when the v2 check does not make it (src/cli/project_v2.rs Amalgam::refusal, B-2026-10-25-4), so every rule on which the two checkers differ refuses a package that a lone file of the same text passes. Whether to bring the per-module typecheck into line rule by rule, or to keep only its module-boundary refusals (private field access across modules and the like), is the owner's call.
fix: a654823884. Kept only the module-boundary refusals. `PackageCheck::past_the_v2_check` (src/cli/build_cmds.rs) runs after the v2 check of the package's combined source has passed, in `karac check` (run_check_cmds.rs) and in `run_v2::combine` for `run`/`build`. It keeps only the per-module type refusals a module boundary carries (`type_error_is_a_module_boundary_rule`: PrivateTypeInPublicSignature, which covers a private field read from another module, and the three NonExhaustiveCrossPackage kinds) and drops the flattened late phases' verdict, which re-checked the same program with the same divergences. A parse, cycle or resolve refusal is untouched. The per-platform and per-target sweeps, which run no v2 check, are untouched too. The row's package (a `ref` to an imported `shared enum` plus `f64.parse("1.5").ok()`) checks and prints `4 1.5` under run, and a private field read from another module is still refused. All nine multi-module example and kata packages check and run the same as before. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs::a_package_is_refused_by_its_modules_only_at_a_module_boundary (control at 2ec14611c4: fails; fixed: passes). Seen while testing, not fixed: `mk().secret` (a private field read through a call's result, the struct not imported) is accepted in a package, before and after this change.

The row's program checks and prints `1 4` under check, run, __mir-run and build. fix: a8cc981ce6 spells the server library's handler `Fn(ref Request) -> Response` (runtime/stdlib/source/http_server.kara). The cause was not the MIR builder: the standard library's own signatures are not D5-rewritten, so the library's `Fn(Request)` was by value there, a closure handler was checked against a by-value parameter, and `__connection` passed it the request by move; a user function handler borrowed because its own bare parameter is rewritten. Both now borrow, and `__connection` reads the handshake key after the handler again (Thread C's original order). Control: the same library with the by-value spelling fails the closure server test in tests/mir_io.rs with the row's move-check error; with the fix mir_io (27), mir_tls_ws (6) and http_server (10) pass. io.md keeps `Fn(Request)`, the user-facing D5 reading.

title: The withdrawn RAII-across-yield pass is dead code: src/raii_check.rs, lib.rs's `raii_across_yield_check`, the `raii_errors` consumers in src/cli.rs / src/cli/diag_json.rs and the `#[cancel_unsafe_until]` attribute surface remain after the pipeline stopped running it
detail: core-semantics §11.9 withdraws `CancelSafe` and `E_RAII_ACROSS_YIELD` (a task is torn down at its wait, so no rule restricts what is held across one). 581bf59ec2 (B-2026-10-25-41, review-thread ruling) took the pass out of the pipeline: `Pipeline::raii_check`, its call in `run_all_checks` and the jsonl `raii_check` phase are gone, tests/raii_check.rs and corpus/fixtures/cli/run_raii_across_yield_violation_aborts are deleted, and tests/cli.rs pins `run_holds_a_shared_value_across_a_network_call`. What is left never runs: src/raii_check.rs (`check_raii_across_yield`, `RaiiAcrossYieldError`), `karac::raii_across_yield_check` in src/lib.rs, the `raii_errors` field of `Pipeline` and the places in src/cli.rs and src/cli/diag_json.rs that read it (always `None` now), and the `#[cancel_unsafe_until]` attribute the pass honoured (src/ast.rs mentions it; `grep -rn cancel_unsafe_until src`). Expected: the code and the attribute surface are removed (Thread A, whose checker it sits in).

fix: fed40c4735. The per-module check never typed a call to an imported function (the name was unbound, so `mk()` was an error type and the field rule never saw `P`). src/typechecker/env_build.rs now binds each imported package function's signature, after registering the types it names from the defining module (`register_transitive_type_deps`), and src/typechecker/fields.rs gives a struct the module neither defines nor imports the module that defines it (`unimported_struct_origin`), in both `check_cross_module_field_access` and `infer_imported_field_access`. `mk().secret` and `let p = mk(); p.secret` are refused with E0221 `private field 'secret' of struct 'P' is not visible outside its defining module`; a `pub` field and the defining module's own read pass. Since B-2026-10-25-46 only boundary rules survive the per-module check past the v2 check, so the newly typed calls add no other refusal: all 9 multi-module packages (selfhost, examples/*, kata 91) check and run unchanged. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_private_field_is_refused_through_an_imported_call` (control at 60e1e5850c: fails).
