detail: In kara-katas apps/cli/mini_pystrich (4ebe77af), `cands.swap((k - 1) as usize, k as usize);` (k an `i64`) passes `karac check` at a654823884, while `Vec.filled(n as usize, 0)` is refused with `implicit coercion from 'usize' to 'i64' would change sign` and a fix that drops the cast. The index checks in src/typechecker/method_vec_mutation.rs (the `check_assignable(&Type::Int(IntSize::I64), ..)` sites at about lines 329, 548 and 594) and the stdlib_seq.rs / stdlib_map.rs / stdlib_iter.rs / stdlib_io.rs equivalents call `check_assignable` alone, not B-2026-10-25-11's `check_i64_arg`, so the sign-change check never runs there. title: A `ref` to a `shared` handle placed in a tuple built by a closure stays `ref S`, so `items.iter().map(|(n, v)| (n.to_string(), v)).collect()` into a `Vec[(String, S)]` is refused (E0200, `FromIterator[(String, ref S)]`), though the same tuple pushed in a loop checks and core-semantics §6.1 counts storing a handle read from a borrow as a value use

`.upgrade()` on a `weak` slot has no working spelling: `a.me.upgrade()` on a `weak` field is "no method 'upgrade' on type 'Option'", though design.md § Cycles and `weak` says `.upgrade()` does the same as reading the field
detail: Split from B-2026-10-25-45 at its close (e0e2a6f136). `shared struct N { id: i64, mut me: weak N }`, `fn main() { let a = N { id: 1, me: None }; a.me = a; println(a.me.upgrade().is_some()); }`: check refuses `no method 'upgrade' on type 'Option'` [E0200], because a read of the field (and since e0e2a6f136 of a `weak` local) is already typed `Option[T]`. design.md: "`.upgrade()` does the same as reading the field, for code that wants to name the `Option` before matching." So a method call whose receiver is a `weak` slot would see the slot's raw type for `upgrade` and yield `Option[T]`. Owner: Thread A (check), who said it would take it later; the builder already upgrades a `weak` place read typed `Option`.
fix: 99e5f3ff2f. The checker records each read of a `weak` slot (a local or parameter, a field, an element), the reads typed the `Option` they upgrade to, in `weak_slot_reads`; `infer_method_call` types `slot.upgrade()` with no arguments, on an Identifier, FieldAccess or Index receiver it recorded, as that read. The builder's `method_call` lowers an `upgrade()` on an `Option` receiver as the receiver's read, which upgrades. `.upgrade()` on any other `Option` is still `no method 'upgrade' on type 'Option'`. The row's program prints `true`; `self.parent.upgrade()` in a `ref self` method, a `weak` local, a `weak` parameter, a `Vec[weak N]` element and a dead referent (`None`) all run on __mir-run, build and the ASan lane. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_weak_slot_upgrade and tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_weak_slot_upgrades_and_passes_to_a_weak_parameter` (control at aa08076a94: fails).

title: Passing a `weak` field straight to a `weak` parameter (`id_of(a.me)` with `fn id_of(p: weak N)`) is refused as "cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place", though the read is a fresh `Option` (an upgrade) and the parameter takes a new weak reference
detail: Found while fixing B-2026-10-25-45 (e0e2a6f136). `shared struct N { id: i64, mut me: weak N }` / `fn id_of(p: weak N) -> i64 { match p { Some(n) => n.id, None => -1 } }` / `fn main() { let a = N { id: 1, me: None }; let w: weak N = a; a.me = w; println(id_of(a.me)); }`: check refuses `error[borrow_projection_copy]: cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place` at `a.me`. Reading a `weak` field yields a counted `Option[T]` made for the read, so nothing moves out of `a`; `let o = a.me; id_of(o)` is the workaround. Same refusal before e0e2a6f136. Owner: Thread A (check).
fix: 99e5f3ff2f. `copy_is_only_an_rc_retain` (src/typechecker/items.rs) counts `Type::Weak` as a counts-only copy, so `warn_borrow_projection_copy` no longer refuses a `weak` field passed to a `weak` parameter. The builder already reads the field through an upgrade and downgrades it into the parameter. The row's program prints `1`, and a dropped referent passed the same way prints `-1`, on __mir-run, build and the ASan lane. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_weak_slot_upgrade (`id_of(a.me)`, `id_of(h.me)`, `via(h.me)`) and tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_weak_slot_upgrades_and_passes_to_a_weak_parameter` (control at aa08076a94: fails).

title: `KARAC_DEBUG_INFO=1 karac build` of any program that spawns a task fails in the LLVM verifier: the call to a coroutine's `#resume` carries no `!dbg` location in a function that has a subprogram
detail: Repro: `fn work(k: i64) -> i64 { sleep_ms(1); k * 2 }` and `fn main() { let g = TaskGroup.new(); let h = g.spawn(|| work(21)); println(h.join()); }`. `karac build main.kara` builds and prints 42. With `KARAC_DEBUG_INFO=1` it stops with `error[mir]: llvm: inlinable function call in a function with debug info must have a !dbg location` / `call void @"kara.main.c0#resume"(ptr %ret, ptr %arg)`, and the same for `--mir` and for every closure task (`c1#resume`, ...). So no task-spawning program can be built with debug info, for a debugger or for symbolized profiles. Found while profiling 10b-3; the workaround there was a no-op `strip` on PATH, since only `strip -x` removes the symbols. Likely cause: src/backend/mir/debug.rs `debug_at` returns early, leaving no location, for a span outside the user's source or at line 0. A body whose builder never got a location (the coroutine piece that calls `#resume`) then emits its call bare. A fix would give such calls a line-0 location in the function's subprogram, or set one at `debug_enter` for synthetic bodies.
fix: f73d059f33. The lowering makes a task's root body (`<task>#task#resume`, and a `par` branch's root), so its span is line 0. `debug_enter` gave it a subprogram, but `debug_at` sets no location at line 0, and none of its statements has a line either, so its call of the task's `#resume` (or the branch closure) went out with no `!dbg` in a function with a subprogram, which the LLVM verifier refuses for an inlinable call. src/backend/mir/debug.rs `debug_enter` now sets a line-0 location in the subprogram for a body at line 0; DWARF reads line 0 as compiler-made code. Located bodies are unchanged, and so is a build without debug info. The row's program builds with `KARAC_DEBUG_INFO=1` and prints 42, and gdb runs it. apps/pipeline/thumb_render (stmt-par, the `.apN` shape Thread B saw) builds with debug info and matches its expected output on 2 workers. 21 of the 23 corpus mir_tasks/mir_select entries build with debug info; the other 2 are refusals that check makes anyway. Pinned by tests/mir_debug_info_tasks.rs (a spawned task and a `par` block, each at -O0 and -O2; in ci.yml's llvm list). Control, the same tree without the fix: both programs fail to build with the verifier message. Gate: fmt, both clippy legs, `cargo test --all`, `cargo test --features llvm` (only the known mir_par_for_iterations_wait_concurrently timing flake and the regex tests, which need the opt-in archive), and mir_tasks + apps/service on mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan (one failure, the pre-existing refusal of mir_tasks_par_branch_break_is_refused, whose expectation comes from legacy-run).

title: Auto-par loops that call into the library run slower than seq on the pool: the compiled program records each library call's place in ONE process-wide global pair (`karac.site` / `karac.site.len`, src/backend/mir/debug.rs), so every worker writes the same cache line before each call (kata 3 0.19x of seq on 4 workers, legacy 2.37x), and an abort on one worker can report another task's call
detail: M4 item 14 timing (Thread B, main ed5750d3ae, 4 CPUs, the kata thread's 92 auto-par loop programs, seq vs KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1 at KARAC_THREADS=4, medians of 3): geomean 2.11x, output identical on all 92, but 10 programs below 0.9x of their own seq build. Kata 3 (sliding_window): seq 23 ms, par4 123 ms wall and 463 ms CPU, all user time. An arrays-only twin of its loop scales 3.2x; the Map version (also with FxBuildHasher) does not. gdb samples sit in karac_hash_word, whose seed statics share a line with the site pair. note_call_site stores the site before every may-abort library call (StrChars.next per char). Marking both globals `internal thread_local global` in the KARAC_MIR_LL output (clang -O2, same archive) gives kata 3 2.82x, 14 2.17x (was 0.92), 17 2.56x (0.55), 71 2.60x (0.96), 394 3.12x (0.81), 3629 2.50x (1.36), 276 4.36x (3.31), all outputs unchanged; estimated 92-program geomean 2.37x, below-0.9x programs 10 to 5 (2, 312, 313, 318, 332, all slow on legacy too: cost-gate cases for item 13). lli-18 runs an internal thread_local under both rtdyld and jitlink on x86_64 Linux; RuntimeDyldMachO is unverified, so the Apple JIT keeps a plain global (the drop schedule's ask).
fix: da5bdc59fc makes `karac.site` / `karac.site.len` thread-local (src/backend/mir/debug.rs site_globals), so each pool worker writes its own pair before a library call and an abort reports its own task's call. On Apple the JIT clears the flag (src/backend/mir/mod.rs compile_mir_ir_for_jit), since RuntimeDyldMachO is not known to link a thread-local; there the pool shares the pair, which costs speed only. Pinned by tests/mir_site_thread_local.rs: the IR holds both thread-local globals, and a program whose four tasks call unwrap at one line while one aborts at another reports the aborting line, built (5 runs) and under karac run, at KARAC_THREADS=4. Control on main fails on the IR check. Measured as in the detail: kata 3 at 2.82x of seq, and the estimated 92-program geomean at 2.37x. Re-timing the full set on main is item 14's write-up.

title: A closure returned from a closure that captures one of the outer closure's own non-`Copy` captures passes `karac check` but the MIR build refuses it: `let base = vec![1, 2, 3]; let make = |n: i64| |x: i64| x + n + base.len(); let f = make(1);` gives `cannot move a non-Copy value out of a borrowed place` (§3.7)
detail: MEASURED on a release build of the B-2026-10-24-9 fix (eede6bfd40): `fn main() { let base = vec![1, 2, 3]; let make = |n: i64| |x: i64| x + n + base.len(); let f = make(1); println(f"{f(0)}"); }` prints `All checks passed.` from `karac check`, while `karac __mir-run` gives `error[mir]: build: 3:25: cannot move a non-Copy value out of a borrowed place: take a copy with .clone(), ... (core semantics §3.7)`. The inner closure is returned, so it escapes and captures `base` by move (core semantics §9.3); the outer closure, whose body therefore moves `base` out of its environment, still captures `base` by `ref` (EnvMode::Ref), so the inner closure's capture is a move out of `(*env).base`. Per §9.1 the outer closure's body moves the place, so the outer capture should be by move too, making `make` a `OnceFn` (§9.4). EXPECTED by that reading, not measured: one call compiles and prints 4, a second call is E0500. Check and the MIR build disagree on the same program, so one of them is wrong; the spec reading above says the build's capture inference is. Not seen when the inner closure captures a `Copy` place, a reference, or the outer closure's parameter (those pass on both, pinned in tests/mir_closure_results.rs). Owner: Thread B (MIR builder capture inference), unverified ownership.
fix: a5ec3ea61c handles closures that return closures in the builder. When a closure's body returns a closure literal (found through the walk note_returned_closures already uses, now `returned_closures_of` in src/mir/lower.rs), each non-`Copy`, non-handle, non-reference place of the outer closure's that the returned closure uses joins the outer closure's moved captures. So the outer closure captures that place by move (§9.1) and its environment is consumed per call (§9.4), and the escaping inner closure's by-move capture (§9.3) no longer moves out of a borrowed environment. A `shared` handle is still counted from the outer environment, which keeps borrowing it. The row's program prints 4 on the interpreter, compiled and ASan. Pinned by tests/mir_closure_returns_closure.rs (a Vec capture; a handle plus a Vec through a block tail with an early `return`), on all three lanes. Control on main: 0 of 2 pass. The checker still accepts a second call or a later use of the moved place, and the build then refuses it with an internal move-check error; that is B-2026-10-26-9 (Thread A).

title: Writing a `mut` field of a captured `shared` handle makes a closure `MutFn` (E0518 at an `Fn` slot), though the capture itself is unchanged and a borrowed-`self` method doing the same write is callable from an `Fn` closure
fix: 0c3f03df1f. The capture is the handle, and a write into the object behind it leaves the handle as it was: any handle may write a `mut` field (core semantics §6.2), as the borrowed-`self` method already could from an `Fn` closure. src/typechecker/core_ref_write.rs (`writes_through_a_handle`) now skips the capture-write mark for a place that projects a field out of a `shared` handle, directly (`cache.stream = ..`, `cache.items.push(..)`) or through a struct field holding one (`b.h.n = ..`). Writing a field of an owned capture, or assigning the handle itself (`cache = C { .. }`), still makes the closure `MutFn`. §9.6 now says so in one sentence. The row's program checks and prints `4` and `3` on `__mir-run`, `__mir-llvm-run` and ASan (clean). Pinned by corpus/core/ok_closure_writes_through_a_captured_handle and tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_closure_writing_through_a_captured_handle_is_fn` (control at 43776f0cec: 0 passed, 1 failed). Corpus check sweep and the 9-package compare unchanged.

title: `karac check` treats a closure that returns a closure as an `Fn` that borrows its captures, when the returned closure escapes and moves a non-`Copy` capture out (§9.3), which makes the outer closure move that place in and an `OnceFn` (§9.1, §9.4): a second call, or a use of the place after the outer closure is made, passes check and the MIR build refuses it with an internal move-check error
detail:
Split from B-2026-10-26-8, whose builder half is fixed. With `let base = vec![1, 2, 3]; let make = |n: i64| |x: i64| x + n + base.len();`:
- `let f = make(1); let g = make(2);` passes `karac check`, and `karac __mir-run` now says `error[mir]: move check main: bb3[term]: use of _4, which may have been moved or never initialized`. §9.6 says a second call of an `OnceFn` is E0500.
- `let f = make(1); println(f"{f(0)} {base.len()}");` passes check, and the build says `move check main: bb4[0]: use of _1 ...`. §9.3 says using the moved place afterwards is E0500, fixed by cloning before the closure.

Both should be E0500 from check, naming `base` and the returned closure. The checker's closure kind (node type `Fn { once }`) and capture modes for the outer closure need the returned inner closure's by-move captures, as the builder now does (src/mir/lower.rs, `returned_closures_of` in closure lowering). Owner: Thread A (check), unverified.
fix: 016b5608ec, with ca82f0ac13. A closure literal returned from another closure (its body's tail, through blocks, `if`, `match`, `return`, tuples, arrays and struct literals) escapes by core-semantics §9.3, so it captures by move, and the outer closure that hands it back moves the capture each call: the outer closure is `OnceFn` when the capture is not `Copy`. src/core_escape.rs walks a closure body as an escaping position ("returned from a closure"), for closure literals only; src/typechecker/closures.rs counts a capture of a returned closure as a consume (`returned_closure_spans`, `capture_walk_by_move`). The row's program runs to `4` with one call; a second call is refused as "an OnceFn is called once", and a use of the capture after is "value 'base' was moved into an escaping closure". ca82f0ac13: such a closure copies a `ref` it captures and MIR keeps that borrow where the result lives (B-2026-10-24-9), so the B-2026-10-25-20 borrow-capture refusal now counts only closures that escape further (core_escape's `closure_result_only`); tests/mir_closure_results.rs passes again. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_closure_returning_a_capturing_closure_is_once` (control 0 passed, 1 failed). Corpus check sweep and the 9-package compare unchanged. Known gap: a closure returned through a call is not followed.

title: `karac check` accepts an escaping closure created inside a loop that captures an outer non-`Copy` binding, which moves it on every iteration; `karac run` stops at an internal MIR move-check error instead of a diagnostic
fix: 647464dbbb. An escaping closure moves its captures in when it is created (core semantics §9.3), so a loop around the creation moves an outer non-`Copy` capture again each iteration (§3.3). Since B-2026-10-25-14 the loop-of-consume rule (src/rc_predicate.rs) skipped a consume inside a capture's closure body, which is right for a loop inside the body but lost the loop around the creation. src/cfg.rs now records each closure literal's creation block (`Cfg::closure_creations`), and the rule checks the loops around it, as it checks a container store's call site, with the same loop-local `let` and rebind exemptions. The row's program is refused as "value 'prog' was moved into an escaping closure ...", with the clone fix, in a `for` and in a `while`, also when the body reads the capture in a loop of its own; MIR's move check refuses the same programs. A clone made inside the loop, a non-escaping closure and a borrowing task closure check and run. Pinned by corpus/core/err_escaping_capture_in_loop and tests/core_strict_check.rs `an_escaping_closure_made_in_a_loop_moves_its_capture_each_time` (control at aec61f30b3: 0 passed, 1 failed). Corpus check sweep and the 9-package compare unchanged.

title: `karac check` counts a capture of an ESCAPING closure as moved when a nested closure in its body reads it (`is.iter().map(|i| look(p, *i)).sum()`, with `p: ref Prog` in `look`): a later read of `p`, or a read in another `match` arm, is 'moved into an escaping closure, used again here', while both MIR backends run it and the same body in a plain function checks
fix: 6f363a1aa2. The capture-scope rule from B-2026-10-25-14 keyed a read inside a nested closure to the innermost enclosing closure, so a non-escaping closure nested in an escaping one (`is.iter().map(|i| xs[i])` inside a closure returned or stored) saw the escaping closure's by-move capture as a move at the read, and a later read in the same escaping body as a use after move. src/use_classifier.rs now tracks which closures on the stack escape (`escaping_closure_flags`) and keys the capture scope to the OUTERMOST closure that takes the name by move, so every read inside its body, nested or not, reads the one captured copy. The apps thread's program runs to `61 21`. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_nested_closure_reads_an_escaping_closures_capture` (control 0 passed, 1 failed). Corpus check sweep and the 9-package compare unchanged.

title: A `shared` handle crosses a task boundary inside a function value: a closure capturing a `shared` struct, erased to `Fn` and captured by a `TaskGroup.spawn` closure, passes `karac check` (E_NOT_CROSS_TASK does not look through `Fn`), and under `KARAC_THREADS=4` its non-atomic count double-frees
fix: 6cfb8ff699. Ruled (review thread, core-semantics §6.3 in e2302c538a): a function value is CrossTask only when everything its environment reaches is, through nested closures and erased `Fn` / `MutFn` / `OnceFn` values. src/typechecker/fn_env_cross_task.rs computes what each function value's environment reaches (closure literals, bindings of them, closures nested in closures, function-typed parameters), and refuses with E_NOT_CROSS_TASK: a TaskGroup.spawn closure holding such a value (the row's program), a function value passed to a parameter that some callee spawns (a fixpoint over calls), and a handler passed to `Server.serve` / `serve_tls` / `serve_ws` / `serve_ws_tls`. The message names the capture and its type; the help points at a `sync` type with `Mutex[T]` or `Atomic[T]` for its `mut` fields. A `sync` store reached through an `Fn`, and a plain capture, still check and run. Thread C moved todo-api and the shortener to a `sync` store first (8d7144c1d8, kara-katas 10b8e29b); the pre-migration versions of both are refused, and b061b33e01 refreshes the corpus shortener copy, which still held the `shared` store. Corpus check sweep otherwise unchanged; 9-package compare unchanged. Pinned by corpus/core/err_fn_value_shared_crosses_task and tests/core_strict_check.rs `a_function_value_reaching_a_shared_handle_does_not_cross_a_task` (six programs; control at b5230d6642: 0 passed, 1 failed).

title: Two `par` branches that walk one `frozen` graph of a `shared struct` race on its reference counts on the pool (KARAC_THREADS=4): ThreadSanitizer reports the count write in the traversal (`kara.sum`, `kara.main.c0`) against `drop.shared Node` on another worker, where core-semantics §6 says a `frozen` handle is never counted and §11.3 lets frozen handles into tasks
detail:
MEASURED with the M4 item 11 lane (`run.py --backend mir-llvm-tsan`, f5689254b4) on a debug llvm karac at f5689254b4 and a TSan runtime archive built with std instrumented (-Zbuild-std=std,panic_abort, RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=thread; CLAUDE.md § Runtime archives). Six runs each, KARAC_HASH_SEED=1, KARAC_THREADS=4, `karac __mir-llvm-tsan source.kara`, exit 86 counted:
- corpus/fixtures/memory_sanitizer/concurrency/asan_frozen_vec_worklist_traversal_across_par_branches_no_leak: 4/6
- .../asan_kata133_clone_graph_bfs_across_par_branches_no_leak: 3/6
- .../asan_frozen_alias_traversal_across_par_branches_no_leak: 1/6 (and fixtures/par_codegen/frozen_alias_traversal_computes_correctly_across_par_branches reported once)
Shape of the report (frozen_alias): `Write of size 8 ... by main thread: kara.sum <- kara.driver.c1`; `Previous write of size 8 ... by thread T1: drop.shared Node <- kara.sum`; location a 72-byte heap block (a Node). vec_worklist: writes in kara.main.c0 / kara.main.c1 (the two branches) against drop.shared Node. So reading a handle out of a frozen value (`let k = n.kids[i]`, `worka.push(g)`, `for ka in na.kids`) counts it and drops it with the non-atomic `shared` count, on two workers at once: a lost update can free a live node.
Not this row: the other reports of the first TSan run (borrow-flag table, stdout buffer, channel queue, all `program_state!` behind a std Mutex) were the archive's precompiled std hiding the lock from TSan; 15 of 17 re-run went quiet with an instrumented std. Outputs are right today (the plain lanes pass), so this shows only under TSan or as a rare crash.
Owner: drop schedule (counting in MIR lowering/drop elaboration for frozen places). Spec: a frozen handle is never counted (core-semantics §6, Gowtham 2026-10-10), so the fix is to not count, not an atomic count. The CI `tsan` leg fails on these until fixed; the pool goes default-on only once it is green (M4 plan item 11).
fix:
dfce639b14. The ownership check's frozen walk already handed over which `let`s are aliases of a frozen place and which `Vec` locals are frozen worklists (OwnershipCheckResult.frozen_alias_bindings / frozen_element_containers, keyed by initializer span), but only the legacy codegen read them; v2 lowering ignored them, so `let k = n.kids[i]` and `q.push(g)` took a non-atomic count. Lowering now carries them (`FrozenHints`) and records each body's frozen locals; `mir::frozen::uncount`, run after the borrow flags, rewrites an alias `x = retain(p)` to `x = &p` (its drops become gotos, a whole use takes its own `retain((*x))`), and a worklist's pushes of `t = retain(q)` to `Vec[T].__push_frozen(&mut c, &q)` (an uncounted copy of the handle) with `Vec[T].__forget_items(&mut c)` before each drop, so the drop frees the buffer and releases nothing (natives in interp.rs and backend/mir/call.rs). A local whose MIR is not that shape keeps its counts: correct, only not count-free.
MEASURED: the 37 corpus programs with `frozen`/`freeze`, `karac __mir-llvm-tsan`, KARAC_THREADS=4, KARAC_HASH_SEED=1, three rounds, instrumented-std TSan archive. Before (at 3232cb4c25): 6 reported every round (the three rows' fixtures, fixtures/par_codegen/frozen_alias_traversal_computes_correctly_across_par_branches, kata 133 clone_bfs_par, fixtures/mir_tasks/mir_tasks_par_branches_each_copy_a_frozen_handle). After: none, except mir_tasks_par_branches_each_copy_a_frozen_handle, which `karac check` refuses (expect = "error:E0512", freeze of a temporary) and which the direct `karac __mir-llvm-tsan` run executes without the ownership check; a lane that honours `expect` judges it as refused. Corpus at 4 workers on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan (apps, core, par, mir_*, concurrency, par_codegen): no new failure (clone_bfs_par's ASan leak is the cyclic clones', red since gate113).
Pinned by tests/mir_frozen_uncounted.rs (the MIR shape, all three backends on one and four workers, TSan five runs each), run in CI's tsan job.

title: E_CHAR_AS_NARROW_INT on an ASCII char LITERAL (`'#' as u8`) carries no edit and its help does not name the byte literal `b'#'`, so `karac fix` leaves each one for the author, though the literal fits and the rewrite is exact (23 hand edits in mini_markdown)
fix: a418ad6c44. For a char literal that is ASCII, cast to `u8`, the typechecker's `Cast` arm (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) now reports E_CHAR_AS_NARROW_INT with "'#' is ASCII, so write the byte literal `b'#'`" and a machine-applicable edit replacing the whole cast. `byte_literal` spells the bytes that need an escape as `b'\''`, `b'\\'`, `b'\n'`, `b'\t'`, `b'\r'`, `b'\0'`, or `b'\xHH'` for any other control byte. A non-ASCII literal (`'é' as u8`) and a `char` value keep the truncation help and get no edit, so the refusal itself is unchanged. The row's program, with a quote, a backslash and a tab added: one `karac fix` run writes the four byte literals, and the result checks and prints `4 233`. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs `an_ascii_char_literal_cast_to_u8_is_fixed_to_a_byte_literal` (control at ab46916012: 0 passed, 1 failed).

title: After B-2026-10-26-14's fixes, at 9030678cd0 `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1` builds still run under the M4b floor of 0.9x their own seq build: on one worker, the default, kata 28 brute_force 0.26x, 191 popcount 0.36x, 4 binary_search_partition 0.56x, 9 palindrome 0.70x and 8 atoi 0.75x (11 programs under 0.9x in all) (CORRECTED: hotel_audit, under on 4 workers in the first three timings, ran 0.97 / 0.98 / 0.92 in three more 21-run timings, inside the swing of a no-site control; no 4-worker app is reliably under at this box's resolution) (Thread B: hotel_audit's two small tasked loops are not the cause either, re-timed in three 31-run passes; the one-worker katas pay for the task form itself, see detail)
detail:
Split from B-2026-10-26-14 at its close. scripts/m4b-speedup.py at 9030678cd0 with fresh archives; results in the shared folder, review/m4b-speedup/.
- 4 workers (m4b-speedup-9030678cd-t4.md, 9 runs; rerun9030a/ and rerun9030b/, 21 runs each): hotel_audit 0.886 / 0.852 / 0.897, 18..24 ms runs with 2 loops, 3 statement groups and 2 reductions as tasks, par cpu/wall 1.14; freight_audit 0.859 / 0.897 / 0.910. The other 7 apps under 0.9x in the 9-run pass crossed 0.9 in a repeat. Katas: none under 0.9x, geomean 2.41.
- One worker, KARAC_THREADS unset (m4b-speedup-9030678cd-t1.md, 9 runs): geomean 0.958 (katas 0.946, apps 0.991), 11 under 0.9x: kata 28 brute_force 0.264, 191 0.359, 4 0.560, 9 0.697, 8 0.747, thumb_render 0.829, 159 0.861, 28 kmp_unchecked 0.866, 393 0.870, 171 0.872, 12 0.889. The identical-binary noise band in that pass is 0.957..1.041. Thread B's harness agrees on 4, 8, 9, 159 and 191 (its message of 2026-10-26); 28 brute_force is not on its list.

The one-worker loss is the parallel form run by one worker, which is what a default `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1` program gets while KARAC_THREADS defaults to 1. Thread B measured wider signed-sum tracking for 4 and 191 and did not land it (numbers in the closed row). Owners: Thread B (builder) for the one-worker katas and hotel_audit's sites, the drop schedule if hotel_audit is the executor's, unverified.

RE-TIMED, three more 21-run timings on 4 workers at 9030678cd0 (rerun9030c/, d/, e/), with sensor_merge (no task site) as the noise control: hotel_audit 0.970 / 0.976 / 0.921; freight_audit 0.857 / 1.031 / 0.911; milk_collect 0.868 / 0.734 / 1.186; risk_batch 0.875 / 1.071 / 0.884; sensor_merge 1.237 / 1.008 / 1.002. On these 5..24 ms programs one 21-run median swings by 0.15..0.45, so the 4-worker half of this row is noise at this resolution; a longer input would be needed to see a few ms. What stays is the one-worker list. THREAD B (10-26, release build at 9030678cd0's successor): hotel_audit, 31 runs on 4 workers, 0.892x as is and 0.978x with its two small tasked loops written as non-counting whiles (revenue_report@782 `for k in 0..4`, a format and push per trip, and ledger_summary@938 `0..min2(5, ..)`), so those 8 calls of 4..5 one-iteration tasks cost about 1.5 ms of 16: a cost-gate question (kata thread). One worker: kata 28 brute_force's sequential build folds the needle (`Vec.filled(16, ..)`) through the heap, and once the needle is captured by a task it escapes, so even the loop as written in the same function loses it; 4, 8, 9, 159 and 191 pay the exact signed-sum tracking per term (an i128 total and both prefixes). Measured, not landed: a pool check that runs an auto-par loop as written on one worker (no gain on 28, 4 or 191, and kata 12 fell to 1.07x on 4 workers); i64 tracking with an i128 fallback (see B-2026-10-26-14). CORRECTED by Thread B (10-26 19:10Z): the 0.892x/0.978x pair was one noisy pass. Three more passes of 31 interleaved runs on 4 workers, same binaries: as is 0.918 / 0.927 / 0.960, without the two loops 0.950 / 1.031 / 0.974. The kata thread's few-trips gate rule also measured no gain (kata-thread/m4-item13-fewtrips-* in the shared folder), so it was not landed. Gowtham's 10-26 12:57Z call puts auto-par default-on together with threads default-on, so one worker is not what a default auto-par program gets. WASM HALF FIXED by Thread B in b657fa3413 (10-27): a wasm build always runs one worker, so `build_source` now builds in order for a wasm target. Kata 28 brute force built with `--target=wasm_wasi` took 6.9 s as tasks and 2.2 s in order (7 runs each under node WASI). Pinned by tests/mir_auto_par_wasm.rs. Native one worker (`KARAC_THREADS=1`, or a one-core host) is still open.

title: `karac check` types a `VecDeque` with `Vec`'s whole method surface, so `d.sort()`, `d.dedup()`, `d.binary_search(x)`, `d.as_slice()` check though collections.md (857e45825) refuses them; it should refuse every method off the VecDeque table with a "no method on VecDeque" diagnostic, suggesting `Vec.from_iter(dq)` for the ones that need one contiguous slice (sort, dedup, binary_search, reverse, ranges, as_slice)
detail: Split out of B-2026-10-21-29 (its fifth part; the other four closed at 4344167c8b). The review thread decided page-vs-checker at 857e45825 (docs/library/collections.md): the VecDeque table now carries new, push_back/front, pop_back/front, front, back, get, len, is_empty, clear, contains, insert, remove (shifting from the nearer end, panicking like Vec's), swap, retain, truncate, extend; try_insert is in the fallible-twins paragraph; iteration, Clone, Display, Eq/Ord and FromIterator are elsewhere on the page. Everything else is refused. The checker today routes VecDeque through `infer_vec_method` (src/typechecker/expr_method_call.rs, the `vec_elem_for_dispatch` block), so the whole Vec surface types. A heuristic scan found no corpus or kata program calling sort/truncate/contains on a VecDeque. Check that the MIR backends implement each table method (insert/remove/swap/retain/truncate/extend on a ring buffer) before closing. Owner: Thread A.
fix: 687ad99102. `karac check` gives a `VecDeque` collections.md's surface (857e45825). `reject_vec_method_on_deque` (src/typechecker/method_vec_mutation.rs), ahead of the aggregate and Vec-mutation surfaces in `infer_method_call`, refuses every Vec/Slice method off the deque table as "no method 'm' on type 'VecDeque'": `push`/`pop`/`first`/`last` carry a machine fix to `push_back`/`pop_back`/`front`/`back`; the methods that need one slice (sort, dedup, binary_search, reverse, as_slice, split_at, chunks, windows, ...) point at `Vec.from_iter(dq)`; max/min/sum/product/join/concat point at `dq.iter().m()`. The page's new methods run on every backend without a new native: contains/remove/swap/retain/truncate are Kāra in runtime/stdlib/source/collections.kara (an element moves by rotating the ring through pop_front/push_back; remove/swap out of bounds panic "index out of bounds"), and `extend` types for a VecDeque and lowers through deque_extend_{iter,vec,set,sorted_set,deque,map,sorted_map} (src/mir/lower.rs extend_from_iterable). Checked on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan with i64 and String elements; every lib:vecdeque corpus entry fails the same on the pre-change binary or passes. Measured over every corpus and kata program naming VecDeque: one newly refused, fixtures/codegen/iter_range/test_e2e_direct_vec_iterator_terminals_survive_being_chained (already refused for `xs.max()` on its Vec), flipped to an error pin. Test: tests/core_strict_check.rs a_vecdeque_has_the_page_surface_not_vecs (control 0 passed 1 failed at 2ee6abbf8e).

title: `karac check` refuses returning a `Vec[(ref Node, i64)]` whose pushed tuples hold a borrow of a parameter ("returned borrowed collection holds an element that borrows function-local storage"), because the pinning check reads the tuple literal `(c, 1)` as a local source; the same push of a bare `c` into a `Vec[ref Node]` passes, and the MIR borrow checker accepts both
detail:
MEASURED 2026-10-27 on main 0a4cfd7fc7 (release karac), Thread B, while pinning B-2026-10-14-29. Prefix `struct Node { val: i64, children: Vec[Node] }`, and `main` builds a one-child tree and prints `frames(t).len()`.

(1) `fn frames(t: Node) -> Vec[ref Node] { let mut v: Vec[ref Node] = Vec.new(); for c in t.children.iter() { v.push(c); } v }`: check passes, runs, prints 1.
(2) the same with `Vec[(ref Node, i64)]` and `v.push((c, 1))`: check refuses at the returned `v` with "returned borrowed collection holds an element that borrows function-local storage; the element's source is dropped when the function returns, leaving the collection's borrows dangling". `karac __mir-run` (which skips check) runs it and prints 1, so the MIR borrow checker accepts it.
(3) `v.push((t, 1))`, a borrow of the parameter itself: the same refusal.
(4) `let local = Node { .. }; v.push((local, 1))`: refused by check, and also by the MIR borrow checker (E0516 drop while borrowed, E0509 result borrows a local), which is right.
(5) `Vec[(i64, i64)]` with `v.push((t.val, 1))`: passes.

CAUSE (read, not bisected): src/ownership/ref_return.rs check_borrowed_collection_pinning classifies each `v.push(src)` source with classify_borrow_return, and a tuple literal is classified as DanglingSource (a literal), whatever its `ref` parts borrow. The tuple's `ref` part should be classified instead, as the bare push in (1) is. The MIR borrow checker already gives the right answer on all five, so the fix is in check only.

TOUCHES: Thread A (src/ownership/).
fix: 098fea6a67. src/ownership/ref_return.rs `check_borrowed_collection_pinning` classified each pushed element (and a returned `Some(..)` / `Ok(..)` payload) whole with `classify_borrow_return`, and a tuple literal reads as a local, so `(c, 1)` and `(t, 1)` were refused. The new `element_source_dangles` takes the element type from the return type (`first_type_arg`) and classifies only the parts at `ref` positions: a tuple literal member by member, a borrowed struct literal by its `ref` fields; a part whose type holds no `ref` is an owned value. Re-measured on the row's five cases: (1) bare `c` passes as before; (2) `(c, 1)` and (3) `(t, 1)` now check and run (`1`); (4) `(local, 1)` is still refused by check, and by the MIR borrow check; (5) `Vec[(i64, i64)]` passes. A nested `Vec[(i64, (ref Node, String))]` with `(1, (t, "a"))` checks too. Pinned by tests/core_borrowed_collection_tuples.rs.

ee104fa4a0 (with d8eb452b1e by Thread B and 95eaaa4f76). Thread B's d8eb452b1e records a function type's declared clause in `Body.fn_value_effects` for each local a call's func operand names and each annotated `let`. src/mir/effects.rs (`declared_fn_value_effects`, used by `call_effects` and `fn_value_effects`) now charges a call through such a local with exactly the declared effects, keyed as classes (`Network` / `FileSystem` as capabilities), plus the default-permitted `panics` and `allocates(Heap)`. No entry is still every effect, per core-semantics §12. The row's repro (`struct Job { run: Fn(i64) -> i64 with reads(Clock) }`, `par { (j.run)(3), (j.run)(4) }`) checks and runs (`25`); the same slot declaring `writes(Stdout)` conflicts on `writes(Stdout)`. 95eaaa4f76 makes the refusal name the unknown's reason (`unknown (a call through a value)`) instead of a bare `unknown`. Pinned by tests/mir_par_stored_callback.rs. Remainder: a call through a captured annotated `let` inside a `par` branch is still unknown, filed as B-2026-10-27-8 (Thread B).
title: A `par` over calls through a stored callback ignores the callback type's effect clause: `struct Job { run: Fn(i64) -> i64 with reads(Clock) }` and `par { (j.run)(3), (j.run)(4) }` is refused as `unknown` and `unknown`, where core-semantics §12 says a call through an escaping function value has the effects its type declares
detail: src/mir/effects.rs charges every call through a value that is not a parameter with `EffectSet::unknown("a call through a value")` (`opaque()`), and the MIR `TyKind::Fn` carries no effect clause, so the field type's `with reads(Clock)` never reaches the analysis. core-semantics.md §12 (line ~699): "A call through an escaping function value has the effects its type declares ... With no effect clause, a call through it has every effect (default 1)." So the clause-less `struct Job { run: Fn(i64) -> i64 }` refusal is right and the clause-carrying one is a false positive. Repro (release karac at 8c794cddcb): `struct Job { run: Fn(i64) -> i64 with reads(Clock) }\nfn sq(x: i64) -> i64 { x * x }\nfn main() { let j = Job { run: sq }; let (a, b) = par { (j.run)(3), (j.run)(4) }; println(f"{a + b}"); }` gives `branches 1 and 2 of the `par` conflict: `unknown` and `unknown``. The diagnostic also names nothing a reader can act on: the set's `why` ("a call through a value") is not printed, so even the correct refusal should say the callback's type declares no effects and how to declare them. Fix: carry the declared clause from the HIR field / binding type into the MIR call site's effects (channel resources as Key::Any), and print the unknown's reason in the conflict message.

fix: 0f5289b733: `strip_main` copies the source a run at a time (from the end of the last `fn main` it skipped), so characters are never split. tests/repl_v2.rs `repl_v2_items_keep_non_ascii_text` pins `héllo, wörld` through an item.
title: The v2 REPL garbles an item's non-ASCII text: `fn greet() -> Str { "héllo" }` then `println(greet());` prints `hÃ©llo`, because `strip_main` (src/repl/util.rs) copied the accumulated items a byte at a time as `char`s
detail: Found while probing B-2026-10-24-1's auto-clone columns, measured at 87001222fe. A cell `let ü = "é"; ...` was refused with the snippet `let Ã¼ = "Ã©"` and an unrelabeled `<repl>:2:5` place, while `karac check` of the same text in a file renders it correctly and a statement cell `println("é")` prints `é`. The cause is `strip_main`, which every cell's, `%show`'s and `:provide`'s program runs the items through: it pushed `bytes[i] as char`, so each byte of a multi-byte character became its own Latin-1 character. Every item holding non-ASCII text (a string literal, a comment, a char) reached the cells' programs changed, so a program's output differed from `karac run` of the same source. Pinned by tests/repl_v2.rs `repl_v2_items_keep_non_ascii_text`.

title: The v2 build refuses `--enable-hot-swap` on a default-profile project and a cross `--target` / `[build].target` by name, where legacy honoured both; 4 cli tests stay ignored
detail: The remainder of B-2026-10-23-16 (closed 392c90770a). That row asked for each flag to work or be refused by name; these two are now refused by name, so nothing is silently ignored, but neither works. (1) `--enable-hot-swap` on a project whose [package].profile is the default: `karac build` stops with `the v2 build does not honour `--enable-hot-swap` yet`. Legacy emitted PLT-style indirection for extern-public module symbols (docs/deferred.md, Continuous PGO with Shared-Object Hot-Swap, commitment 1). The wasm and embedded/kernel refusals already match legacy's wording. Ignored: tests/cli.rs test_build_project_hot_swap_accepted_with_default_profile. (2) A cross `--target=<triple>` (or `[build].target` in the manifest) naming a non-host triple: refused with `the v2 build does not honour a cross `--target` yet`. src/backend's MIR object emission uses the host target machine. Ignored: test_build_target_flag_activates_overlay_dep, test_build_target_space_separated_form_parses, plus test_build_target_from_manifest_build_section and the `--target` sibling at tests/cli.rs ~15888, each of which passes only where the target is the host. Owner for (2) is the backend (drop schedule) together with the cli driver.
fix: 6be9fd1111: both now work on v2. (1) A cross --target / [build].target triple is built for, not just used for the overlay as legacy did (legacy linked a host binary): the object is compiled for the triple (Target::initialize_all on that path only, so a host build's time is unchanged), linked with KARAC_LINKER, else the triple's GNU cross gcc on PATH (x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu), else clang --target=<triple>, against the runtime archive built for the triple (KARAC_RUNTIME, else <karac>/../lib/<triple>/, else target/<triple>/release/); a missing archive fails at the link naming `rustup target add` and the cargo rustc recipe. The triple also picks the [target.<triple>.*] overlay, the walk platform, the CPU baseline arch and the .exe suffix; codegen-unit splitting is off for a cross build. Measured: hello.kara --target=x86_64-pc-windows-gnu on Linux gives a PE32+ x86-64 hello.exe (tests/build_v2_target.rs checks MZ / PE / machine 0x8664 when mingw and the archive are present). (2) --enable-hot-swap on a default profile: each non-generic module-scope pub fn (main aside) gets a slot in the external karac_hotswap_table [N x ptr]; __karac_init_hot_swap_table in llvm.global_ctors fills it; each direct call of a registered body loads its slot and calls through it, taking the callee's final param/return/function attributes (noalias is marked after lowering, so they are copied at the end) and calling convention (src/backend/mir/hot_swap.rs). Flag-off IR is byte-identical (KARAC_MIR_LL diff). Still refused on wasm (now also a wasm32-* triple) and embedded/kernel. The 4 ignored cli tests run (a cross build on a host without that triple's archive is accepted when it stops at the link with the recipe, after the overlay walk they pin) and the two cfg-gated ones run on every host; tests/project_v2_refusals.rs's cross [build].target refusal pin is flipped.

title: On the pool (threads on by default since 72ce9e026c), sleepers wake out of deadline order: the first park opens the reactor's epoll set under the executor's lock, and its F_DUPFD to descriptor 100 grows the fd table, which in a threaded process waits out an RCU grace period (48 ms under strace), stalling every worker; a 60 ms sleeper woke before 20 and 40 ms ones
detail: Found when tests/mir_reactor.rs's sleepers test went red in a gate after default-on (mir_reactor_sleepers_wake_in_deadline_order_beside_a_parked_task, 1 in 6). Built program, 100 runs on 4 cores: 76 in order, 14 with the 60 ms sleeper before the 40 ms one, one with it before the 20 ms ones. Timestamps showed the tasks spawned after the first park starting 13 to 21 ms late, all at once. strace -f -tt: fcntl(ep, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, 100) took 48 ms (expand_fdtable synchronizes RCU when the file table is shared by threads), inside park() -> Reactor::watch under the shared EXEC lock. A second, smaller hole: idle_wait read the timer heap and the running count under two locks, so a sleeper another worker settled in between was missed until the wait's old deadline; and a napping first worker was not roused by a new timer.
fix: 808e37ce9b. Reactor::open (runtime/src/mir_task.rs) makes the epoll set and moves it to descriptor 100. start_workers calls it before spawning any thread, so the fd table grows while the process has one thread and skips the RCU wait. watch() calls the same open() lazily, which is all the one-worker executor needs. Two smaller holes closed in the same change: idle_wait reads the timer heap and the running count under one lock (a worker settles its sleeper before it stops counting as running, so with none running every timer is already in the heap), and settling a Wait::Until / FdBy task rouses a napping first worker. Measured on 4 cores, the row's program built: 76/100 in deadline order before, 200/200 after, with task starts at 0 ms instead of 13-21 ms late. New pin tests/mir_reactor.rs mir_reactor_pool_sleepers_wake_in_deadline_order (KARAC_THREADS=4; deadlines 20/60/100/140 ms). Four tests that pinned print order across tasks now run their build on one worker (§11.1, §11.9): the same-deadline sleepers, mir_isolating_built's natives and teardown, and mir_cancel_running_and_unstarted_tasks. Task suites (34 files, 349 tests) clean 7 runs in a row.

title: The v2 wasm build always emits a core module: `--bindings=component` (the wasm_wasi project default) does not embed the WIT world or componentize, `[toolchain] wasm-tools` is never consulted, and a `host fn` imports from `kara_host` instead of the canonical-ABI `kara:<pkg>/host`; 2 cli tests ignored

title: A `let p: P = Json.deserialize(s).map_err(f)?` (or `.context(msg)?`) is refused with "cannot infer type parameter 'T' of `Result[T, DeserializeError]`": the annotation on the `let` does not reach the receiver of a method whose `Ok` type is the receiver's, through the `?`
detail: MEASURED 2026-10-27 on main 87001222fe plus the B-2026-10-21-22 fix (debug karac --features llvm), Thread A. Program: `import std.json.{Json};` `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] struct P { x: i64 }` `fn go(s: String) -> Result[i64, String] { let p: P = Json.deserialize(s).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; Ok(p.x) }` and a `main` that calls `go(Json.serialize(P { x: 3 }))`. `karac check` says: "cannot infer type parameter 'T' of `Result[T, DeserializeError]`, this call's result: nothing in the body fixes it (design.md § Type inference); bind the result with a type annotation" at the `Json.deserialize(s)` call. The same with `.context("reading P")?` into a `Result[i64, AnyError]`. Binding the call first (`let r: Result[P, DeserializeError] = Json.deserialize(s); let p = r.map_err(...)?;`) checks and runs (prints 3). `map_err[F]` returns `Result[T, F]` and `context` returns `Result[T, AnyError]`, so the `?`'s value is the receiver's `T`, which the `let`'s `P` fixes; the checker does not carry the expected type back through the method's return type to its receiver. design.md § Type inference is bidirectional within a function body; whether a method's receiver is inferred from its result is the question (INFERRED that it should, since the `let`-then-call form needs no new information).

title: A `par` branch that calls a captured, annotated `let` (`let f: Fn(i64) -> i64 with reads(Clock) = ..; par { f(3), f(4) }`) is still refused as `unknown (a call through a value)`: the declared clause reaches a call through a field and through a let in its own body, not through a capture
detail: Remainder of B-2026-10-27-2. d8eb452b1e records a function type's declared clause in `Body.fn_value_effects` for each local a call's func operand names and each annotated `let`, and src/mir/effects.rs (`declared_fn_value_effects`) charges a call through such a local with exactly those effects. A `par` branch is a closure body, and a `let f` it captures is reached through the closure's environment, so the call's func operand is (inferred, not dumped) a projection of the env parameter with no entry, and the call keeps every effect. `(j.run)(3)` on a captured struct works because the builder copies the field into a temp local first. Repro: `fn sq(x: i64) -> i64 { x * x }\nfn pick(n: i64) -> Fn(i64) -> i64 with reads(Clock) { sq }\nfn main() { let f: Fn(i64) -> i64 with reads(Clock) = pick(0); let (a, b) = par { f(3), f(4) }; println(f"{a + b}"); }` gives `branches 1 and 2 of the `par` conflict: `unknown (a call through a value)` and ...`, where core-semantics §12 gives the call the effects its type declares. Pinned by `mir_par_stored_callback_captured_from_a_let_is_refused_for_now` (tests/mir_par_stored_callback.rs, PREDICTS). Fix: carry the clause for a func operand that is a capture (builder), or copy the capture to a local with an entry.

fix: 75990e74c3. `karac check` reads each impl method's parameter and return types against its trait method's at the impl (src/typechecker/items.rs, check_impl_signatures_match_trait): `Self` is the impl's type, `Self.A` the impl's own binding, the trait's generics its trait arguments, and the method's generics the impl method's by position. The row's program is now refused: "the return type of impl method 'S.mk2' is `Option[i64]`, but trait 'Mk2' declares `Option[bool]` there". An impl associated type the trait does not declare is refused ("defines associated type 'B', which 'Tr' does not declare"), and a parameter-count mismatch too. Only types known on both sides are compared: a projection, an inference variable, or an `impl Trait` against a concrete type is taken to agree, and an `impl Trait` against an `impl Trait` compares the trait and its bindings. Modes stay §4.7's check, and a function type's parameter modes are compared under the mode, since D5 rewrites user `Fn(A, T)` to borrow and leaves the library's owned. Pinned by tests/core_impl_signature.rs (4 tests; on the base tree 3 fail and the accepting one passes). Corpus check sweep: 21 new refusals before two fixes (impl-side `Self`, Fn parameter modes), 0 after, apart from the twelve operator traits. DELIBERATE GAP: the operator traits (Add .. Shr, Neg, Not) are skipped, because the library declares them without the spec's `Rhs` and `Output` and every operator impl binds an `Output`; check_operator_output already holds the method's return to it, and the rest is B-2026-10-27-13.
title: An impl method's signature is not checked against its trait's: `impl Mk2 for S { type A = bool; fn mk2(self) -> Option[i64] { Some(7) } }` under `trait Mk2 { type A; fn mk2(self) -> Option[Self.A]; }` passes check, and `fn get[T: Mk2[A = bool]](t: T) -> bool { t.mk2().unwrap() }` prints `7` for a `bool`; an impl binding an associated type its trait does not declare (`type B = bool`) is accepted too

A trait impl's method named like an inherent method of the same type shares its MIR instance name (`Bag.into_iter`), so a call through the bound (`c.into_iter()` under `C: IntoIterator`) runs the inherent body: prints 7 where the trait impl's body gives 100

`Iterable` (design.md § `Iterator` and `Iterable`, a lang-item trait: `type Item; fn iter(self) -> impl Iterator[Item = Self.Item]`) does not exist, so `for x in c` over a user collection cannot borrow it: `impl Iterable for Bag` is 'undefined type Iterable'

Passing a function value held in a collection element to a non-escaping function-typed parameter (`apply(v[0], 4)` over `fn apply(f: Fn(i64) -> i64, x: i64)`) is refused as a move out of the element, where core-semantics §4.1 / §9.3 make a bare `Fn` parameter a borrow
detail: Measured at dcd242dbc8 plus the B-2026-10-22-43 fix: `fn doubler(n: i64) -> i64 { n * 2 }\nfn apply(f: Fn(i64) -> i64, x: i64) -> i64 { f(x) }\nfn main() { let mut v: Vec[Fn(i64) -> i64] = Vec.new(); v.push(doubler); println(f"{apply(v[0], 4)}"); }`. `karac check` gives `cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a collection element: the collection still owns it` (src/use_classifier.rs walks the argument as Consuming: the bare `Fn` parameter's mode is owned in the front end's tables), and the MIR builder refuses the same call independently (`borrow check main: ... move of (*_17) through a shared reference [E0517]`), so the program cannot run on any path. Before the B-2026-10-22-43 fix check passed it and only the MIR refusal remained. The non-function control `fn size(s: String) -> i64 { s.len() }` with `size(w[0])` over a `Vec[String]` checks and runs. core-semantics §9.3: function-typed parameters are non-escaping by default and the callee may only call them or pass them on; §4.1: an argument to a borrowed parameter moves nothing. A local `let f: Fn(..) = doubler; apply(f, 1); apply(f, 2)` already works, because check reads a function value as `Copy`. Fix: give a bare (non-`escaping`) function-typed parameter the borrowed mode in the front end's call modes and pass it by reference in the MIR builder, together.

title: The library's operator traits are declared without the spec's `Rhs` parameter and `Output` type (runtime/stdlib/add.kara: `trait Add { fn add(own self, rhs: own Self) -> Self; }`; design.md § Operator Traits: `trait Add[Rhs = Self] { type Output; fn add(own self, rhs: own Rhs) -> Self.Output; }`), so an operator impl's signature cannot be checked against its trait: `impl Add for I { type Output = I; fn add(own self, rhs: own D) -> I }` (the spec needs `Add[D]`) passes check and `I + D` runs
